name: Jasch Gauging Technologies Ltd.
industry: Industrial metrology - on-line non-contact thickness, basis-weight and coating-weight gauging systems
business: Jasch Gauging Technologies took over the demerged industrial-gauges division of Jasch Industries and manufactures on-line, non-contact measurement systems - beta/nucleonic, X-ray, infrared and laser thickness, basis-weight, moisture and coating-weight gauges - at its works at 43/2 Bahalgarh Road, Sonipat (Haryana), with the registered office in Pitampura, Delhi. The systems are mounted on running paper machines, plastic film and extrusion lines, steel and non-ferrous rolling mills and coating lines, and are sold with commissioning, calibration and spares service (FY26: product sales Rs 56.27 cr, service Rs 1.19 cr). FY26 revenue from operations was Rs 57.46 cr with PBT of Rs 19.91 cr; the company is debt-free and declared a Rs 10 per share interim dividend for FY27 in July 2026. It is a real manufacturer with in-house electronics, sensor and systems assembly.
import_substitution: Named and company-confirmed. The FY26 annual report states plainly that 'similar products (industrial thickness gauges) are not being manufactured in India at this scale', so the alternative supply for an Indian paper mill or film line is an imported gauging system from the US, UK or Japanese incumbents - Thermo Fisher Scientific (USA), NDC Technologies/Nordson (UK/USA) and Yokogawa or Toshiba-class systems (Japan). Every gauge Jasch installs is a system an Indian mill would otherwise have had to import, along with its foreign-currency spares and service contract.
moat_note: Regulator-conferred plus installed-base lock-in. Beta/nucleonic gauges use sealed radioactive sources, and their manufacture, possession, transport and disposal in India require AERB licensing - a licence very few Indian firms hold, which is the practical reason the annual report can say no one else makes these at this scale. On top of that, once a gauge is integrated into a paper machine's control loop, replacement means re-qualifying the whole measurement and control chain, so customers stay for the calibration and spares annuity. ROCE 21.3% and a 26% OPM on a debt-free balance sheet are consistent with a genuine barrier.
why_obscure: Demerged out of Jasch Industries and listed only on BSE (no NSE line), so it is invisible to NSE-only screens; it is routinely confused with the parent, a synthetic-leather maker that sits on many exclusion lists. No earnings call, no investor presentation, no sell-side coverage, zero FII and zero DII, and the only forward-looking statement management has ever made is buried in a Section 197 remuneration disclosure in the annual report.
risk_note: Pure capital-goods cyclicality with no annuity cushion large enough to offset it. The FY26 annual report attributes 'inadequacy of profits' directly to 'the cyclical slowdown in the capital goods sector', and PAT was flat at Rs 14.74 cr against Rs 14.68 cr with three-year sales and profit CAGRs both negative (-5% and -4%). Other income of Rs 5.80 cr is about 29% of the Rs 19.91 cr PBT, so operating profit is only ~Rs 14 cr; one soft order year - and Q4 FY26 PAT already dropped to Rs 2.98 cr from Rs 5.14 cr in Q2 - takes earnings down 30%+ with no revenue diversification to absorb it.
liquidity_note: BSE-only mainboard microcap at Rs 238 cr with 42.37% float and 7,324 holders. Daily traded value is small and there is no NSE leg, so entry and exit both require patience; the Rs 10 interim dividend does provide a yield anchor.
cwip_note: Nil CWIP across all three years and a net block of only Rs 9 cr against Rs 57 cr of revenue - this is an asset-light, engineering-and-assembly business, not a capex story. Reserves of Rs 94.69 cr against Rs 4.53 cr of equity capital means the balance sheet is mostly cash and receivables.
guidance_quote: 'The Company expects improvement in its operational and financial performance by 10% to 20% over the next 1-2 years supported by a stronger order pipeline and ongoing efficiency initiatives.'
guidance_source: Jasch Gauging Technologies FY26 Annual Report, dated 25 May 2026 - 'Other information' disclosure under Part II Section II of Schedule V of the Companies Act, 2013
score_rationale: AERB source licensing plus control-loop re-qualification switching costs, backed by 21.3% ROCE and a company statement that no one else in India makes these at scale, earns 18/25 - held below 20 only because it is a domestic licensing barrier rather than a USFDA/CE-class one. Import substitution is company-confirmed against named foreign incumbents: 16/20. Promoter 57.63% is dead centre of the 55-70% peak band and unchanged year on year: 13/15. Zero FII and zero DII: 2/15. BSE-only listing, 7,324 holders, no calls or coverage, constantly confused with the excluded parent: 13/15. ROE 15.7%, zero debt, but negative three-year sales and profit CAGR: 8/10. Total 70.
warnings: Three-year sales (-5%) and profit (-4%) CAGRs are both negative; the guidance is for recovery, not growth from a rising base.
Other income is ~29% of PBT, so headline profitability overstates operating earnings.
Zero institutional ownership and no NSE listing - price discovery is poor.

The AERB-licensing and named-competitor points are analytical attributions, not company disclosures - see verify_comment.

name: Global Pet Industries Ltd.
business: Incorporated 2013; manufactures automated PET stretch blow-moulding machines (3-6 cavity configurations, 2,400-10,500 bottles/hour) used by bottling and packaging plants to make PET bottles/containers.
import_substitution: PET stretch blow-moulding machines are a classic import category — historically dominated by European (Sidel/Krones) and Chinese (Jomar, Sipa-clone) suppliers; a small domestic manufacturer offering mid-capacity machines at lower cost substitutes imports for India's fragmented bottling/FMCG packaging SMEs that cannot justify a full European line.
moat_note: Blow-moulding machine design requires precision mould-and-clamp engineering and servo/hydraulic tuning know-how; an installed base creates a spares/service annuity, though barriers to new entrants in this niche are moderate rather than high.
why_obscure: Tiny free float (537 shareholders) and sub-Rs 200cr market cap PET-machine maker with zero analyst coverage, invisible next to plastics-machinery names like Kabra Extrusiontechnik or Windsor Machines that dominate searches.
risk_note: Single-product-line dependency on PET packaging capex cycles; very thin shareholder base could mean poor secondary-market liquidity; no debt-to-equity disclosed.

name: Beezaasan Explotech Ltd
business: Incorporated in 2013, manufactures industrial explosives and explosive accessories — slurry and emulsion explosives, detonating fuse and cast boosters — sold to cement, mining and infrastructure customers, and to defence-adjacent buyers including the Border Roads Organisation (BRO) and other PSUs.
import_substitution: Bulk and packaged industrial/blasting explosives and detonating accessories in India have traditionally been supplied by a small number of PSU/licensed private manufacturers rather than imported (explosives are heavily import-restricted for safety/security reasons); Beezaasan is one of the few private-sector manufacturers licensed to supply BRO and other government/PSU users domestically, substituting for scarce PSU-only production capacity rather than a specific import line.
moat_note: Explosives manufacturing requires PESO (Petroleum & Explosives Safety Organisation) product and factory licensing, magazine storage licenses and security clearances — a real regulatory barrier to entry — plus established relationships with BRO/mining-PSU procurement channels that are slow to requalify new vendors.
why_obscure: Small-cap explosives maker with under 1,000 shareholders and essentially no analyst or media coverage; overshadowed in investor attention by the larger listed peer Premier Explosives.
risk_note: 3-year sales have actually declined (-2% CAGR) even as profit grew, suggesting margin/mix-driven earnings rather than volume growth; small scale, thin free float, and explosives-industry safety/regulatory risk (licence suspension, accident liability) are real tail risks.
penalty_detail: only 937 shareholders - effectively no secondary market (-7)
cwip_note: The FY25 capex bulge (CWIP ₹12cr) has been capitalised — net block rose ₹37cr → ₹50cr and CWIP fell back to ₹3cr.
data_note: Flat/lumpy: FY26 halves replicate FY25 exactly and full-year PAT slipped ₹14cr → ₹13cr. P/E read between 54 and 62 across fetches.

name: Gandhi Special Tubes
business: Makes small-diameter seamless and welded precision steel tubes and cold-formed coupling nuts, sold per metre with heavy cold-draw and bright-anneal value-add. 85% of revenue is seamless tube whose flagship application is diesel fuel-injection lines, sold to leading Indian and global OEMs. FY26 sales Rs 192 cr against net PPE of only Rs 41.5 cr; the big capex was in 2006 and 2012. Runs 5.35 MW of captive wind plus 2 MW solar (69% renewable energy) and carries zero debt.
moat_note: Company-stated in a statutory document. The FY26 annual report says under Strengths: 'Preferred supplier — the only local player of comparable scale and quality approved by most leading Indian and global OEMs.' The note observes this is 'company-stated, in a statutory document, with no market-share number anywhere.' No certifications are cited. The evidence offered instead is economic: the margin is explained by four separable, verifiable causes from the FY26 P&L — raw material only 34% of sales; a written-down asset base (net PPE Rs 41.5 cr against Rs 192 cr of sales, depreciation 1.8% of sales); captive renewables; and employee cost 5.1% of sales with zero debt.
pricing_power_note: Pricing power — strong but cyclically peaked. OPM 36% to 36% to 38% to 40% to 44% (FY22-FY26). 'But in the FY20 downcycle OPM went 37% to 30% and sales fell 34%. FY26 was two simultaneous upcycles (CV and tractor). Q4 FY26 OPM already fell to 41.3% from 46.0% in Q3. Treat it as a structurally 33-38% business currently earning 44%.'
import_substitution: Yes, in company-stated form: the FY26 annual report describes Gandhi as 'the only local player of comparable scale and quality approved by most leading Indian and global OEMs' — i.e. the sole domestic supplier at that scale and quality level, though no market-share number is given anywhere.
why_obscure: Low institutional footprint — 13,841 holders and institutional holding of 1.28% against a 1.00% Tier 1 threshold, which the note calls 'fragile, but correct today'.
risk_note: Terminal value: 85% of revenue is seamless tube whose flagship application is diesel fuel-injection lines, and BEV and CNG powertrains delete this part entirely, with no product roadmap disclosed. name: NGL Fine-Chem Ltd.
business: Makes active pharmaceutical ingredients for veterinary medicine — anthelmintics (albendazole, oxyclozanide, closantel), antibacterials and antiprotozoals — plus a smaller human-API book. Manufacturing sits at Tarapur MIDC and Navi Mumbai in Maharashtra, with a large new Tarapur greenfield block under commissioning. Exports run to roughly 70 countries; the customer base is animal-health formulators in the EU, LatAm and South-East Asia rather than named Indian pharma majors. Veterinary API is a niche the large Indian API houses have largely ignored.
import_substitution: Replaces Chinese-origin veterinary anthelmintic APIs — specifically albendazole, closantel and oxyclozanide — where China holds the bulk of world capacity. NGL is one of a very small number of non-Chinese producers of these molecules at scale, and global animal-health customers explicitly buy it as a China+1 source.
moat_note: EU-GMP and WHO-GMP certified sites with CEP/EDQM-route filings for its lead veterinary molecules; veterinary API registration dossiers in the EU take years and are customer-specific, so switching cost is real. Backed by an 18.6% ROCE.
why_obscure: Veterinary API is not a category any Indian sell-side desk covers; the stock has no earnings call, no investor presentation and 13,393 shareholders. Screeners classify it under 'Pharmaceuticals' where it disappears among 300 names.
risk_note: Single-niche concentration — a price collapse in albendazole/closantel driven by Chinese restart would hit both volume and spread simultaneously, and the Mar-2025 loss quarter shows how thin the buffer is.
liquidity_note: Mainboard NSE/BSE but a ~Rs 3,040 share price on a small float means daily traded value is typically well under Rs 5 cr; building a position takes weeks.
cwip_note: CWIP has near-doubled from Rs 50 cr to Rs 95 cr and now stands at ~58% of net block — the largest capex cycle in the company's history and clearly still rising.
score_rationale: Highest-quality name in this sweep: regulator-conferred EU-GMP/CEP barrier in a niche China dominates, 18.6% ROCE, 37% 3Y profit CAGR, a 58%-of-net-block capex cycle, and PAT that has turned decisively positive after the Mar-25 loss. Docked on institutions (0.07% combined is effectively zero) and on moat (veterinary, not USFDA human-API, so short of the 20+ band).

name: Fermenta Biotech
business: Makes Vitamin D3 and nutrition ingredients, backward-integrated into cholesterol at its Dahej plant, plus a premix plant at Kullu. 73% of revenue is one molecule. Serves 400+ customers in 60+ countries, including UN rice-fortification tenders via WFP approval. An Indian process patent for plant-source vegan D3 (VITADEE Green) was granted in September 2025. Family-controlled since 1951; audited by SRBC & Co, an EY member firm.

The FY26 annual report states twice: 'Among the world's top 3 manufacturers of Vitamin D3', and the Chairman's letter adds that Fermenta 'until very recently was India's only manufacturer of Vitamin D3 in any form.' The note calls this structurally plausible — 'pharma-grade D3 globally is DSM, BASF, a couple of Chinese producers and Fermenta' — but 'not independently verified by a rating agency.' The real evidence is the certification stack, 'the deepest in the cohort, and all of them gate a market': EU-GMP and US-FDA (Dahej), EDQM CEP for Vitamin D3 100 SD secured in FY26 (opens EU regulated pharma), WHO-GMP, FSSC 22000, BRCGS, HACCP, NSF, FAMI-QS, KLBD Kosher, Halal, AVA/Vegetarian Society UK, RSPO, WFP approval for UN rice-fortification tenders and a GAIN Letter of Approval for the Kullu premix plant.

Quarterly trend is currently deteriorating: 18.2% to 16.5% to 14.8%.
import_substitution: Yes, in company-stated form: the Chairman's letter says Fermenta 'until very recently was India's only manufacturer of Vitamin D3 in any form', and the company claims to be among the world's top 3 D3 manufacturers. Neither statement is independently verified.
why_obscure: Low discovery — 14,131 holders and institutional holding of only 0.17%; it passes the v3 gates as Tier 2.
risk_note: The moat does not defend the margin: two loss-making years in the last four when Chinese D3 prices collapsed, and the clean-margin history is shorter than the reported one because FY23-FY25 reported EBITDA was flattered by real-estate 'value unlocking' worth 9-18% of revenue, which fell to 0.4% in FY26. name: High Energy Batteries (India) Ltd.
business: Part of the SPB (Seshasayee) group, based in Mathur, Tamil Nadu, manufacturing reserve and secondary batteries for strategic applications: Silver-Zinc, Nickel-Cadmium and Silver-Chloride-Magnesium (sea-water activated) systems for torpedoes, submarines, missiles, aerospace and space launch vehicles. FY26 revenue was ₹83.5cr, essentially all from the Aerospace/Naval/Power System Batteries segment (the Lead Acid division has been suspended since April 2019). Concretely it has indigenised silver-zinc torpedo batteries and 120kW silver-chloride-magnesium sea-water activated light-weight torpedo batteries previously sourced from European suppliers.

name: Dhabriya Polywood Ltd.
industry: Plastic Products / uPVC Profiles, Doors & Windows
business: Jaipur-based extruder and fabricator selling under the Polywood brand. Two revenue engines: a B2B PVC-profile distribution business that is over 60% of revenue (it extrudes and sells profile to independent window fabricators), and a project business that fabricates and installs uPVC windows and doors, WPC doors, PVC false ceilings and wall panels, modular furniture and now aluminium windows and facades for builders. Plants at Jaipur and Bengaluru, with a new Jaipur aluminium/facade factory under construction. Order book of Rs 74 cr as of May 2026, the highest in its history; customers are developers in Maharashtra and Delhi-NCR, not individually named in filings.
import_substitution: uPVC window and door profile - India's premium profile market was built on imports and licensed European systems (Rehau, Deceuninck, Veka from Germany/Belgium) plus low-cost Chinese profile. Dhabriya extrudes profile domestically and sells it to fabricators, displacing the imported-profile route at the mid-market end.
moat_note: Contestable. The barrier is a fabricator/dealer network built over two decades plus in-house extrusion (most window fabricators buy profile, they do not make it), which gives vertical margin. There is no certification lock; a competing extruder can be set up with capital. The 20% EBITDA margin comes from a deliberate product-mix shift up-market, not from a structural moat.
why_obscure: Rs 634 cr mainboard microcap with 7,032 shareholders and essentially no institutional sponsor (FII 1.51%, DII 0.45%). It sits in 'plastic products' on screens, so window-and-door investors never find it and plastics investors think it is a pipe company.
risk_note: The project half of the business is at the mercy of builder scheduling, and management has already been burned by it: FY26 growth undershot its own 20-25% target purely because uPVC window supplies to large Maharashtra and Delhi-NCR projects were deferred at the developer's end. At 42.5x on roughly Rs 30 cr of PAT, a repeat deferral is a de-rate, not a delay.
liquidity_note: BSE/NSE mainboard but a genuine microcap - Rs 634 cr with a ~30% public float and no institutional anchor means daily traded value is modest and the stock gaps on results.
cwip_note: CWIP jumped from Rs 0.32 cr (Mar 2025) to Rs 6.33 cr (Mar 2026) against an Rs 88.4 cr net block - only 7% of net block, so this is not a heavy-CWIP story. The build is the new Jaipur aluminium-window/facade factory plus a WPC door line, against a stated Rs 27 cr FY27 capex programme.
score_rationale: Import substitution 13 - the imported product (uPVC window profile) and origins (Germany/Belgium systems, Chinese low-cost profile) are named, but Dhabriya competes at the mid-market rather than replacing the premium imports head-on, so it stops short of 15. name: Clay Craft India Ltd.
business: Clay Craft India is a Jaipur-based manufacturer of bone china and porcelain tableware and crockery, selling under its own brand into Indian retail and HoReCa channels and supplying OEM/export orders. Bone china requires bone-ash body preparation and a two-stage high-temperature firing cycle, which is why the Indian producer set is small. Public filings do not name individual customers or retail chains, so none are asserted here.
import_substitution: Displaces imported Chinese bone china and porcelain tableware, which has historically dominated the mid-market Indian crockery shelf. The imported product and origin country are both identifiable (bone china / porcelain tableware from China), though Clay Craft does not quantify the share it has taken.
moat_note: Process know-how plus brand. Bone china firing has a narrow window - warping, crazing and translucency defects punish sub-scale operators - and a 24% OPM against commodity ceramic peers is the evidence that this is not a generic kiln business. Backed by 20% ROCE. It is not, however, a resource or regulatory monopoly: Chinese capacity can re-price the shelf at will.
why_obscure: NSE SME listing with only 2,039 shareholders, no analyst coverage, no earnings call, and a consumer-durables classification that buries it among tile and sanitaryware names it has nothing to do with.
risk_note: Chinese import pricing. This is a discretionary consumer product with a 24% OPM defended largely by cost and duty differentials; a renewed dumping cycle or a cut in effective import duty on ceramic tableware compresses that margin directly, and there is no contracted order book to cushion it.
liquidity_note: NSE SME (Emerge) - lot-size constrained, wide spreads, and 2,039 holders means genuine liquidity risk on exit. This is a name you can only size small.
cwip_note: CWIP Rs 2 cr (FY24) -> Rs 0 cr (FY25) -> Rs 2 cr (FY26) against Rs 104 cr net block. No expansion cycle visible; reserves have compounded from Rs 112 cr to Rs 152 cr over the same window, so cash is being retained rather than deployed into new kilns.
guidance_source: Document search for Clay Craft India management revenue-growth commentary returned no company-specific transcript, presentation or MD&A chunk. As an NSE SME the company does not hold earnings calls. No guidance to cite.

name: Alufluoride Ltd.
business: India's largest producer of Low Bulk Density Aluminium Fluoride (AlF3), a critical fluorine chemical additive used by primary aluminium smelters (Vedanta, Hindalco, NALCO) to reduce the melting point of alumina in the Hall-Heroult electrolysis process.
import_substitution: AlF3 is a strategic input for India's aluminium smelting industry that historically required imports (from China and the Gulf) to supplement domestic supply; Alufluoride is the largest domestic AlF3 producer, directly reducing smelters' reliance on imported fluoride chemicals.
moat_note: Fluorochemical process technology plus proximity/long-term supply contracts with India's major aluminium smelters create a durable, hard-to-replicate domestic supply position; global AlF3 market is fragmented and freight-cost-sensitive, favouring local producers.
why_obscure: Sub-Rs 350 cr market cap fluorochemical niche supplier with negligible FII/DII holding and no broker coverage.
risk_note: Single-product concentration (AlF3) tied entirely to aluminium smelting capex/output cycles in India; input fluorspar largely imported, so it is exposed to raw-material import risk even while displacing finished-product imports.

name: DMCC Speciality Chemicals Ltd. (formerly Dharamsi Morarji Chemical Co. Ltd.)
business: One of India's oldest chemical manufacturers (established 1919 as Dharamsi Morarji Chemical Co., recently rebranded); pivoted from legacy sulphuric acid/phosphate fertiliser production to a fully-integrated specialty chemical platform built on sulphur, boron and ethanol chemistry — sulfonation, sulfation, chlorosulfonation, Friedel-Crafts, esterification and ethylation reactions — supplying textile, polymer, dye, pharma, water-treatment and agrochemical intermediate customers; recently invested ~Rs 90 cr in capex at Dahej.
import_substitution: Sulfonated/chlorosulfonated specialty intermediates for dye, pharma and agrochemical customers are frequently import-sourced from China; DMCC's century-old hazardous-chemistry capability (concentrated sulfuric acid/oleum handling) at legacy sites positions it to displace some of that import volume, though the company does not disclose specific substitution figures.
moat_note: Genuine hazardous-chemistry capability — sulfonation/chlorosulfonation and oleum handling — built over 100+ years of operating experience, plus environmental clearances at established sites (Ambernath, Roha, Dahej) that would be very difficult for a new entrant to replicate given India's tightened EC/CTE approval regime for sulfonation units.
why_obscure: Recently rebranded from Dharamsi Morarji Chemical — one of India's oldest listed chemical names hiding in plain sight under an unfamiliar new ticker most investors have not reconnected with.
risk_note: FII holding roughly halved year-on-year (1.16% to 0.15%), signaling reduced institutional confidence; company is mid-pivot from legacy fertiliser business to specialty chemicals, carrying execution risk; capex-heavy expansion (Dahej) adds near-term leverage/return risk.
cwip_note: CWIP is lumpy and small (₹6cr FY24, nil FY25, ₹5cr FY26) at just 2.3% of a ₹220cr net block — no major capex cycle visible.
data_note: Management explicitly refuses to guide. MD Bimal Goculdas, 25 May 2026 call: “It's really my style not to give futuristic projections.” Q1FY27 PAT of ₹20cr is a 2.5x step-up on the ₹6–8cr band held for seven quarters.

name: Voith Paper Fabrics India Ltd.
industry: Paper machine clothing / industrial technical fabrics
business: Formerly Porritts & Spencer (Asia), this is the Indian arm of Germany's Voith Group and makes paper machine clothing - the forming fabrics, press felts and dryer fabrics that carry the wet web through a paper machine - from a single mill at Faridabad, Haryana. It also makes fibre-cement sheet-making felts and high-tech textile-processing felts, and describes itself as the only manufacturer in India offering the complete range of machine clothing. FY26 revenue Rs 208.9 cr (+9.8%) and PBT Rs 55.2 cr, with Rs 38.5 cr of that revenue exported through fellow Voith companies in the US, China, Malaysia, Sweden, Spain, Brazil, Chile and Argentina. Zero debt, 27% operating margin.
import_substitution: Substitutes imported paper machine clothing - historically forming fabrics and press felts brought in from Voith Austria/Germany, Albany International (US) and increasingly low-cost Chinese PMC makers. Voith Paper (China) Co. Ltd is a named related party from which the Indian entity still buys traded goods (Rs 78.3 cr in FY26), so the substitution is partial: it localises manufacture of the core range while still importing specialty grades from China and Europe.
moat_note: Paper machine clothing is a consumable specified per machine: the fabric is engineered to a given machine's width, speed, drainage profile and furnish, trialled on the mill, and then reordered on a fixed replacement cycle. A mill will not re-trial a fabric supplier to save a few percent because a failed fabric means an unplanned machine stop. Add Voith Group technical know-how (Rs 9.0 cr of know-how fees paid to JM Voith SE in FY26) and this is a genuine, customer-conferred barrier - just one earning 14.9% ROCE, not 25%.
why_obscure: A 74%-owned subsidiary of a private German engineering group with 5,188 shareholders, no earnings call, no investor presentation, and a Rs 646 cr market cap. It is still tagged 'PORRITSPEN' in some data feeds, which breaks screens. Nothing in the disclosure regime forces it to talk to investors and it does not.
risk_note: Its end market is the Indian pulp and paper industry, which the company's own annual report describes as facing rising imports and raw-material cost inflation; the global pulp and paper market is projected to grow at only ~1.7% CAGR to 2035. FY26 PBT grew just 2.8% and absorbed a Rs 5.1 cr hit from the new labour codes. A single-mill, single-end-market business with a 74% parent also carries permanent minority-squeeze/delisting risk at the parent's timing, not yours.

name: Jasch Industries Ltd.
industry: PU/PVC coated fabrics and polyurethane resin
business: Makes PU and PVC coated fabrics (synthetic leather) plus polyurethane resin at Sonipat, Haryana, and is backward-integrated into PU resin, which it both consumes captively and sells to adhesive and coating customers. Its own annual report states it is 'the only significant manufacturer of PU Synthetic Leather' in India, where almost every other unit makes PVC leather only. FY26 revenue Rs 228.8 cr split roughly 51% PU / 49% PVC, with PU segment revenue up 42% and PU segment profit up 134% year on year. End uses are footwear uppers, linings and insoles, garments, automotive seat covers, furniture upholstery, bags and sports goods. A second plant (Unit-2, village Bhigan, Sonipat) with imported machinery is due to start commercial production by end-October 2026, adding 115 lakh metres/year of PVC coated fabric.
import_substitution: Directly substitutes PU synthetic leather imported from China. The FY26 annual report is explicit: the Indian synthetic-leather industry 'has not been able to achieve its full potential due to tough competition from imported material from China, where there are very large units enjoying benefits of economies of scale'. Jasch's defence is its captive PU resin plant - it is the only Indian producer with in-house PU chemistry, and breathable PU grades for automotive are called out as an under-competed opportunity.
moat_note: The barrier is technical rather than regulatory: in-house PU resin manufacture, which nobody else in the Indian synthetic-leather industry has, plus breathable-PU know-how for automotive and garment applications where PVC cannot compete. This is real but contestable - a Chinese supplier with scale can undercut it any quarter, and Jasch has no evidence of formal OEM IATF qualification the way Mayur does. Scored accordingly.
why_obscure: Rs 191 cr market cap, BSE-only, 6,485 shareholders, zero institutional holding, no earnings call and no investor presentation. Its second business line - electronic thickness gauges - makes it look like an unclassifiable conglomerate to screens. The consolidated page on Screener is stale (last populated around FY23), which silently drops it out of automated scans.
risk_note: Raw-material squeeze plus execution risk on a plant that will roughly double PVC capacity. The FY26 Board Report states that towards the end of FY26 'the prices and availability of petroleum-based raw materials and gas have been adversely affected, resulting in pressure on margins' and that the company 'has not been able to fully pass on' the increase. Against that, management has budgeted a 50%+ revenue jump for FY27 on a business with D/E already at 0.6 and Rs 23 cr of CWIP against a Rs 39 cr net block - if Unit-2 slips past October 2026 or PU spreads stay compressed, the budget misses badly and the balance sheet has less room than the 12.8x P/E implies.
liquidity_note: BSE microcap at Rs 191 cr with a 42% public float and 6,485 holders. Thin but not untradeable for small sizes; expect wide spreads and multi-day exits. Exact traded value not verified.
cwip_note: The heaviest CWIP-to-net-block ratio in this batch by a wide margin: CWIP Mar 2024 Rs 0 cr, Mar 2025 Rs 5 cr, Mar 2026 Rs 23 cr against a Rs 39 cr net block - 59%. This is Unit-2 at Bhigan, land acquired and plant imported, commercial production guided for end-October 2026. Installed PU coated-fabric capacity was separately raised from 30 to 40 lakh metres/year for only Rs 1.3 cr. The asset base is about to expand ~60% in one step.
guidance_quote: Adopting forward looking approach despite the current geo-political climate, the management has budgeted revenue of Rs. 345 crore during the financial year 2026-27, representing an increase of over 50% over the preceding financial year.
guidance_source: Jasch Industries FY26 Board Report / Annual Report, filed 25 May 2026
score_rationale: Top import-substitution score of the batch at 16 - the company itself names the imported product (PU synthetic leather) and the origin country (China) in its own annual report, and its structural answer (sole Indian captive PU resin capacity) is verifiable. Moat 13, not higher: technical differentiation without customer- or regulator-conferred qualification, and a Chinese competitor can reprice it. Promoter 13 on 57.64%, dead centre of the ideal band. Institutional 2 - literally zero FII and zero DII. Undercovered 13 on 6,485 holders and no coverage of any kind. Financials 7 despite ROE of 18.9% because the 3-year profit CAGR is negative (-13%) and D/E is 0.6.

name: Anuh Pharma Ltd.
business: Founded 1960 and part of the SK Group, Anuh is among the world's largest producers of first-generation erythromycin salts, and also makes corticosteroid, anti-TB, anti-malarial, antibiotic and anti-diabetic APIs. The single plant is at MIDC Tarapur (Boisar, Palghar), where installed capacity was lifted from 2,200 MT to 2,400 MT in FY26, with R&D at Mahape, Navi Mumbai. It exports to over 85 countries and serves 1,200+ customers. FY26 revenue was Rs 776 cr, up 16%, though PAT fell to Rs 41 cr.
import_substitution: Substitutes Chinese-origin macrolide antibiotic APIs — specifically the erythromycin salt family (erythromycin stearate, estolate, ethylsuccinate) — where China dominates fermentation-derived supply. Newer launches Vildagliptin, Dapagliflozin propanediol monohydrate and Allopurinol likewise displace Chinese API imports into regulated markets.
moat_note: USFDA and EU-GMP approvals on the Tarapur site plus EDQM Certificates of Suitability specifically named in the FY26 annual report for Allopurinol (CEP) and Sulphadoxine (SDD CEP) — a regulator-conferred barrier, and scale leadership in erythromycin salts that took six decades to build.
why_obscure: Only recently obtained an NSE listing alongside its long-standing BSE line, has no analyst coverage or earnings call, zero institutional register, and a Rs 76 share price that keeps it off institutional screens entirely.
risk_note: Margin, not volume, is the problem — OPM has compressed to 8% and FY26 EBITDA fell to Rs 66 cr on 16% higher revenue, so global API price erosion is landing directly on the P&L despite growing tonnage.
liquidity_note: Mainboard on both exchanges but with essentially no institutional participation; a Rs 760 cr cap with 27,484 retail holders means thin, retail-driven turnover.
cwip_note: CWIP is nil and has been for six straight years; the FY26 capacity addition from 2,200 to 2,400 MT was a debottleneck within the existing Tarapur block, so this name offers guidance rather than capex as its kicker.
guidance_quote: We are tremendously charged-up with growth potential for our existing products and newly introduced products. We expect to grow between 15-20% in FY27.
guidance_source: Bipin N. Shah, Vice Chairman — Vice Chairman's Message to the Shareholders, Anuh Pharma FY2025-26 Annual Report, filed 19 May 2026

Promoter stake rose 188 bps. Scored down severely on institutions (0.01% combined is effectively zero) and on financials, where 8% OPM, 10.7% ROE and a 3% 3Y profit CAGR are genuinely weak.

name: Energy-Mission Machineries (India) Ltd.
business: Incorporated 2011, Ahmedabad-based designer and manufacturer of CNC, NC and conventional metal-forming machines under the 'Energy Mission' brand - hydraulic press brakes, shearing machines, plate rolling machines, hydraulic presses and fibre laser cutting systems. It also runs a B2B e-commerce platform for aftermarket spares and consumables, which is unusual for a machine builder of this size. Customer base is fabrication job shops and sheet-metal SMEs across Gujarat, Maharashtra and the north; individual named customers are not disclosed.
import_substitution: CNC press brakes and sheet-bending / shearing machines, a segment where Indian fabricators otherwise buy Amada (Japan), Trumpf and Bystronic (Germany / Switzerland), Durma and Baykal (Turkey), and increasingly low-cost Chinese brands. India imports a large share of its CNC forming machine consumption; this is a named, origin-specific substitution play.
moat_note: Machine tools are sold on installed base, application engineering and nationwide service response, not on certification. Switching cost is real once a fabricator's operators are trained on a control platform and spares logistics are set up, but a determined Chinese or Turkish importer can contest any single order - moat is commercial, not regulator-conferred.
why_obscure: NSE SME listing (IPO 2024), 1,687 shareholders, half-yearly reporting, Rs.139 cr market cap, and no sell-side coverage. Screens keyed to 'capital goods' rarely reach NSE Emerge names of this size.
risk_note: Demand is levered to small-fabricator capex, which is the first thing to be deferred in a credit tightening or a steel-price shock; a Rs.18 cr CWIP block is being funded partly with debt (D/E 0.31) into that cyclicality.
liquidity_note: NSE Emerge (SME) scrip; SME lot-size trading with thin daily turnover. Realistic position sizing is small and exit takes days, not minutes.
cwip_note: CWIP has risen three years running - Rs.1 cr, Rs.7 cr, Rs.18 cr - and now stands at 51% of the Rs.35 cr net block, indicating a new manufacturing facility under construction rather than routine maintenance capex; this is the heaviest genuine CWIP-to-net-block ratio in the batch after AMIC.

name: Agarwal Toughened Glass India Ltd.
business: Rajasthan-based glass processor. Buys float glass and converts it into toughened/tempered safety glass, heat-strengthened glass, laminated glass and insulated glazing units for building facades, doors, shower partitions, railings and shopfronts. It is a converter, not a float-glass melter - the furnace-side economics belong to its suppliers. No named customers are disclosed in filings, so none are asserted. Listed on NSE Emerge.
import_substitution: Processed architectural safety glass (toughened and laminated) landed from China and Malaysia. The substitution is real but partial - the float substrate itself is still largely bought in, so only the conversion step is domesticated.
moat_note: The most defensible barrier in this batch: safety glass for building use must be certified to BIS IS 2553, which is a regulator-conferred licence, and processed glass is heavy, fragile and expensive to freight, which hands each certified processor a de-facto regional catchment. The 23% ROCE is consistent with that. It is still only regional - it does not travel.
why_obscure: NSE SME with 1,031 shareholders, half-yearly reporting only, listed 2024, and a business (glass conversion) that has no listed peer set for analysts to benchmark against.
risk_note: It is a converter squeezed between a float-glass oligopoly upstream (Saint-Gobain, Asahi India, Gold Plus) and price-taking fabricators downstream - it does not set its own input price. The FY26 second half already showed the squeeze from the other side: PAT fell from Rs 12 cr (H1FY26) to Rs 9 cr (H2FY26) even on higher sales, because the effective tax rate went from about 20% to about 35%. The SME tax tailwind is spent.

business: Incorporated 2015, JD Cables makes LT/HT power cables, control cables, aerial bunched (AB) cables and ACSR/AAAC conductors for the power transmission and distribution sector from two units (Unit I and Unit II) running at ~82.4% and ~84.6% utilisation in FY26. name: Laxmi Dental Ltd.
industry: Dental devices - laboratory prosthetics, clear aligners, aligner raw material, intraoral scanners
business: India's only end-to-end integrated dental products company: custom dental laboratories making crowns, bridges and removable prosthetics; Bizdent clear aligners; Vedia aligner raw material (thermoforming sheets and blanks); intraoral scanner sales; and paediatric dental products. Labs and plants sit in Mumbai (Boisar and Mira Road) and Kochi, with roughly 33-34% of revenue exported, largely to US and international dental labs. FY26 revenue was Rs 277.9 cr, up 16.2%, with EBITDA margin 15.6% and PAT margin 10.4%; the company launched iScope 360, a remote dental scanning/consultation platform, in Q4 FY26 and reports ~80% digital penetration in its Indian dental business. It genuinely manufactures - the lab prosthetics and aligner raw materials are made in-house - but the intraoral scanners it sells are bought-in hardware.
import_substitution: Partly named: Vedia supplies aligner-grade thermoforming sheets and aligner raw materials that Indian and international aligner makers otherwise import from US and German specialty suppliers (Bay Materials/Zendura class material, Scheu-Dental type sheets); the dental-lab business also repatriates prosthetic work that US and European clinics would otherwise source from Chinese labs. Against that, the intraoral scanners the company resells are imported hardware, so the import-substitution story is real but only partial.
moat_note: Export-market regulatory clearances are the barrier: US FDA registration and CE marking for the aligner and prosthetic lines, ISO 13485 quality system, plus MDR-compliant lab processes. Management explicitly calls out 'aggressively pursue export certifications' as a FY26 investment. On top of that sits scanner-installed-base lock-in - a dentist running a Laxmi scanner routes prosthetic and aligner orders back through the Laxmi platform, a razor-and-blade switching cost management describes as a 'win-win'.
why_obscure: It is not obscure - this is the weakest leg of the case. The company IPO'd in January 2025, hosts Motilal Oswal-run earnings calls, and carries 30.1% FII and 10.9% DII holding with 36,937 retail shareholders. It sits inside the screen only because holders are still under 40,000 and the promoter is above 40%; the market follows it closely.
risk_note: US tariff exposure on roughly a third of revenue. Management confirmed the company is currently paying about 10% tariff on US exports and that a half-quarter of tariff cost alone cut Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin by ~74 bps. A step-up in the US tariff line, or the intensifying domestic aligner price war management flagged in FY26, hits a business already running at 16% OPM and 31x earnings.
liquidity_note: Mainboard NSE and BSE, Rs 1,091 cr market cap with institutions holding 41% - the most institutionally liquid name here, and consequently the least mispriced.
cwip_note: Nil CWIP across Mar 2024, Mar 2025 and Mar 2026. FY26 capex of about Rs 18.4 cr (per the Q4 concall) was capitalised directly; IPO proceeds earmarked for capex remain undeployed, so no CWIP signal.
guidance_quote: Sameer Merchant, MD & CEO: 'if you see what we have done in the last couple of years... last to last year was 24%. This year was 16%. Even in the situation, which was tough. So, we don't see a challenge that over the next two, three years; we should grow at a similar trajectory.' He immediately declined to be pinned to a number ('No, no, I am not commenting on that number').
guidance_source: Laxmi Dental Q4 FY26 earnings conference call, 22 May 2026 (transcript filed 30 May 2026)
score_rationale: FDA/CE/ISO 13485 clearances plus scanner-driven switching costs justify 17/25, held below 20 because ROCE is only 14.9% - the regulatory barrier is not yet translating into superior returns. Import substitution is real (Vedia sheets) but partial and the company itself imports scanners, so 13/20. Promoter at 41.8% is far below the 55-70% peak band: 7/15. FII 30% + DII 11% is 41% institutional - well past the 2-15% band the rubric rewards, i.e. already discovered, so 8/15. 36,937 holders plus active broker coverage caps obscurity at 4/15. ROE 14.8%, near-zero debt, 124% 3Y profit CAGR off a low base: 8/10. Total 57.
warnings: 36,937 shareholders is within 8% of the 40,000 gate - a single good quarter could push it out of the screen.
Promoter 41.8% offers almost no cushion above the 40% gate.
Already well covered (Motilal Oswal-hosted calls, 41% institutional) - this is a quality name, not an undiscovered one.

name: Kalyani Cast-Tech Ltd.
business: Incorporated 2012, Delhi-headquartered (Okhla) manufacturer of steel castings and specialised ISO cargo/shipping containers. Management's FY26 shareholder letter states the company crossed Rs.152 crore revenue and became, by a significant margin, the largest container manufacturer in India. It broke ground during FY26 on a 144-acre integrated manufacturing and logistics campus in Gujarat and has stated an intent to enter railway wagon manufacturing. Named end customers are not disclosed in public filings.
import_substitution: ISO marine and specialised cargo containers, a product category in which roughly 95% of world supply is Chinese (CIMC, Dong Fang, CXIC). Indian container buyers — shipping lines, CONCOR-type operators, logistics firms — have historically bought Chinese boxes; this is a direct, named substitution of Chinese imports.
moat_note: Container manufacturing needs CSC plate certification and classification-society/lessor approval per box design, plus very large fabrication footprint and steel throughput — the scale barrier is real, but the product itself is globally commoditised, so the barrier is contestable rather than regulator-locked.
why_obscure: BSE SME board listing, only 2,209 shareholders, no broker coverage, half-yearly reporting, and the business sits in a 'containers/logistics' bucket that industrial-goods screens rarely surface.
risk_note: Promoter stake fell 3.84 percentage points in twelve months (63.31% to 59.47%) while the company simultaneously commits to a 144-acre greenfield campus — dilution/selling into a heavy capex cycle is the single biggest risk.
liquidity_note: BSE SME scrip at ~Rs.618 cr market cap; SME lot-size trading, thin two-way depth, and exit is genuinely difficult in size. Treat as a position that cannot be unwound quickly.
cwip_note: CWIP rose from nil to Rs.3 cr in FY26 as ground was broken on the 144-acre Gujarat campus; the reported balance-sheet CWIP badly understates the announced project, so the capex is rising but not yet capitalised.

name: Dr. Agarwal's Eye Hospital Ltd.
business: The originally listed entity of the Dr Agarwal's eye-care group, running a chain of eye hospitals concentrated in Tamil Nadu. FY26 sales Rs 471 cr with 31% OPM on a cataract-plus-refractive surgical model supplemented by opticals, contact lenses and eye-care pharma. Group-level FY26 disclosure (which this entity feeds) shows 288 facilities across 10 countries, 3,23,245 surgeries and 30.09 lakh patients served, with 968 doctors. This entity is under an NCLT-supervised merger into the larger listed parent Dr. Agarwal's Health Care Ltd (AGARWALEYE); shareholder and creditor meetings were convened on 2 July 2026.
import_substitution: None - domestic services play. Phaco systems, femtosecond lasers and IOLs are imported inputs (Alcon, J&J, Zeiss); the company consumes them rather than replacing them.
moat_note: The strongest regulator-and-brand barrier in this batch: NABH-accredited hospital scope, a 1957-vintage clinical brand in Tamil Nadu, and a captive network of 968 group ophthalmologists - eye surgery is a supply-constrained speciality where the surgeon roster, not the real estate, is the scarce asset. 31% operating margin on Rs 471 cr, alongside the group being the largest eye-care chain in India by both revenue and surgical facilities, evidences pricing power rather than tender-taking. Referral density inside a single state also compounds: 182 of 288 group facilities sit in the South.
why_obscure: It is the wrong ticker. Sell-side, index funds and screens all follow the Rs 13,000 cr+ parent AGARWALEYE listed in 2025; this legacy BSE line trades at Rs 5,349 a share, has 22,954 holders and is being absorbed by merger, so most desks treat it as a stub not worth modelling. A Rs 5,349 share price also mechanically excludes it from retail screens.
risk_note: Merger-ratio risk dominates everything else. This entity is mid-way through an NCLT scheme to merge into Dr. Agarwal's Health Care Ltd; the swap ratio, not operating performance, will set the realised return, and an unfavourable ratio or a scheme delay at the NCLT Chennai bench would strand holders in an illiquid stub. Secondary risk: D/E has gone to 0.96 (borrowings Rs 326 cr vs equity Rs 346 cr) with lease liabilities of a further Rs 244 cr, while CWIP of Rs 197 cr is not yet earning.
liquidity_note: Mainboard-listed but BSE-only in practice and very thin: 23.03% public float on Rs 2,585 cr, at a Rs 5,349 share price, with institutions holding only 4.29% combined. Daily traded value is small for the market cap and the merger overhang suppresses turnover further. This trades like a microcap despite the headline number.
cwip_note: The heaviest CWIP ratio in this batch. Audited FY26 balance sheet shows CWIP Rs 197.32 cr against Rs 127.98 cr a year earlier, and PPE of Rs 172.65 cr plus right-of-use assets Rs 202.17 cr. On the screener net-block basis of Rs 403 cr, CWIP is 48.9% of net block; measured against owned PPE alone it exceeds it. Three straight years of build (Rs 97 cr, Rs 128 cr, Rs 197 cr) means a large tranche of assets is capitalised but not yet generating - do not annualise current ROCE forward without hair-cutting for that.
guidance_quote: Looking ahead, we expect to sustain growth at a similar pace to the prior year, underpinned by deeper penetration of existing micro markets, expansion into new geographies and the accelerated adoption of innovative surgical procedures and advanced technologies across our network.
guidance_source: Dr. Agarwal's Health Care Ltd Q4/FY26 earnings call, 27 May 2026 (parent entity into which DRAGARWQ is merging). FY26 revenue from operations grew 21.6% YoY, so 'a similar pace' implies roughly 20%+. Same management team; the scheme is at NCLT.
score_rationale: 63/100. Only name here to earn 20 on moat - NABH-accredited multi-site eye-care scope backed by 31% OPM, 17.4% ROCE and a 968-doctor network, which is a genuine regulator-plus-clinician barrier rather than contestable contracting. Import-sub 3, correctly near zero. Promoter 12 not 14: 72.67% sits above the 55-70% sweet spot. Institutional 12 on FII 2.24% + DII 2.05% = 4.29% combined. Undercovered only 8 - 22,954 holders and the group is heavily covered via the parent, even if this line is not. Financials 8: ROE 25.2% and 24% 3Y profit growth are strong but D/E 0.96 caps it.
warnings: Under NCLT merger into Dr. Agarwal's Health Care Ltd - the swap ratio, not operations, drives the outcome.
The guidance quote is a PARENT-level statement from the merging acquirer, not a standalone DRAGARWQ target. Treat as group-level.
D/E 0.96 plus Rs 244 cr of lease liabilities; Rs 197 cr of CWIP is not yet earning.
Hospitals are capex-heavy with long gestation - the Jun 2026 spike to Rs 23 cr PAT is one quarter, not a trend; the prior four quarters were 17/19/17/16.
22,954 shareholders is the highest count in this batch, so the undercovered edge is the weakest here.

name: Tanfac Industries
business: Fluorine chemistry — anhydrous hydrofluoric acid and aluminium fluoride, with technology licensed from Davy Process and CHENCO. name: Cords Cable Industries Ltd.
business: Incorporated 1991, Cords makes the narrow end of the cable market: control cables, instrumentation cables, thermocouple extension/compensating cables, data cables and power cables up to 3.3 kV, including fire-resistant, low-smoke-zero-halogen and low-temperature variants, from plants in Rajasthan (Bhiwadi/Kaharani). End markets are process industry and infrastructure — power generation, refineries and petrochemicals, steel, cement, metros and railways — supplied largely through EPC contractors rather than direct branded sales. This is the only genuinely specification-driven cable maker in this batch: instrumentation and thermocouple cable is engineered to a customer datasheet, not sold off a price list.
import_substitution: Named but unverified: high-specification instrumentation, thermocouple and low-smoke-zero-halogen cable in Indian refinery and power projects was historically supplied by European makers — Lapp and Helukabel (Germany), Nexans (France/Belgium) and Belden (US/Netherlands) — and Indian control-cable makers have been substituting that spend for two decades. I could NOT find this substitution claimed in Cords' own filings (no earnings call or investor presentation exists in the document database), so this is an industry-structure inference, not a company-confirmed one, and it is scored in the generic band accordingly.
moat_note: The barrier is customer-conferred approval, not scale: instrumentation and thermocouple cable has to be type-approved and vendor-listed by the EPC/owner (EIL, L&T, refinery and utility owners) against a specific technical datasheet, and requalifying a cable supplier mid-project is disruptive — real switching cost. But a 17.7% ROCE and 6% OPM show the approvals are not translating into pricing power; the customer base (EPC contractors) captures the margin.
why_obscure: 18,046 holders on a Rs 311 cr mainboard name, no analyst coverage, no earnings call and no investor presentation anywhere in the filings database — a document search returned nothing under this company. It is a 35-year-old listed company that the market has simply stopped looking at; the shareholder count actually FELL from 19,409 to 18,046 over the year.

name: SKP Bearing Industries Ltd.
business: Incorporated 1992, Jaipur-based manufacturer of precision needle rollers, cylindrical rollers, pins and balls - the rolling elements that go inside needle roller and cylindrical roller bearings. name: Envirotech Systems Ltd.
business: Incorporated 1997, Envirotech Systems is a B2B noise-pollution-control engineering house that designs, fabricates and installs acoustic enclosures, engine test-room acoustics, noise booths, acoustic louvres/doors, fire-retardant acoustic doors and highway noise barriers. import_substitution: Anechoic and semi-anechoic NVH test chambers and precision acoustic test booths are a category India has historically imported as turnkey systems from Bruel & Kjaer (Denmark), Eckel Industries (USA) and IAC Acoustics (UK). Envirotech builds these domestically. The substitution is inferred from the product category, not from a company disclosure naming a displaced import, so it is graded weak rather than solid.
moat_note: Not regulator-conferred. The barrier is acoustic design capability plus the fact that an anechoic chamber must be validated to ISO 3745 / ISO 26101 free-field criteria before an OEM lab can use it for homologation data. Once a chamber is installed in a customer's test lab, replacement cost and re-validation make switching expensive. Ordinary acoustic enclosures, which are the volume business, are contestable by any fabricator.
why_obscure: NSE SME board, listed only recently, 1,425 shareholders, no sell-side coverage, no earnings calls in the filings database. It sits in an industrial-products bucket rather than a 'green' bucket, so environment screens miss it and industrials screens ignore a Rs 138 cr fabricator.

(Italy); Taslan yarn commercial production has started, and a greenfield needle-punch non-woven line is targeted for Q3 FY27.
import_substitution: Weak as an India-facing substitution story - this is an export-led business, not an import replacement. The genuine substitution elements are the two new lines: Taslan textured PP yarn produced under the Essegomma S.p.A. (Italy) JV, replacing Italian and Chinese textured yarn used in outdoor furniture, upholstery, luggage and automotive interiors; and the needle-punch non-woven line aimed at geotextile, artificial-leather backing, exhibition carpet and shoe-insole substrate currently imported from China.

But FIBC itself is a crowded Indian export industry with dozens of certified players and the product is priced off PP resin. Genuine but contestable, and the certification does not confer pricing power.

It publishes quarterly investor presentations but has no analyst coverage and 7,552 holders.

A reversal in PP granule spreads or European freight would take margins straight back toward 5-6%, and at 10% EBITDA margin with 70% export exposure a 5-7% adverse EUR/INR move is enough to halve PAT. name: Shri Jagdamba Polymers Ltd.
industry: Geotextiles and woven PP technical fabrics
business: Ahmedabad-based maker of woven and laminated polypropylene technical textiles, described by itself as 'textile fabrics impregnated, coated, covered or laminated with plastic'. Product range: geotextile, silt fence, lumber cover, roofing underlayment, PP woven ground cover, tarpaulin, PP woven bags, BOPP-laminated bags and box bags. The construction-and-landscape products (silt fence, lumber wrap, roofing underlayment, ground cover) are essentially US-market specifications and are exported; the woven sack and BOPP bag lines serve the domestic food, fertiliser and cement trade. A large capacity addition ran through FY25 (Rs 42 cr CWIP) and has now been capitalised into a Rs 154 cr consolidated net block.
import_substitution: Partial. Domestically, PP woven geotextile, silt fence and ground cover displace Chinese woven geotextile and ground cover that Indian road, irrigation and horticulture contractors otherwise import. But the higher-value construction range is built to US specifications for export, so the company is as much an exporter as a substituter, and the domestic mix is heavily commodity woven sacks.
moat_note: Thin. Product-level approvals for geotextile/roofing underlayment in US construction channels give some qualification stickiness, but woven PP fabric is a converting business with low technical entry barriers and hundreds of Indian competitors, and it shows in the numbers: 13.0% ROCE and 12% OPM. There is no OEM panel, no BIS/technical mandate that a competitor cannot also obtain, and no evident switching cost. This is technical textiles by product code more than by economics.
why_obscure: Filed under plastics rather than textiles, no earnings call, no investor presentation, and - confirmed by document search - not a single filing indexed in the standard research corpus. 6,964 shareholders and a BSE-primary listing. A US construction slowdown or a tariff action on Indian woven fabric would strike the profitable half of the mix.

business: Atha group company manufacturing Calcined Petroleum Coke (CPC) on a pure B2B model, selling to aluminium smelters, graphite-electrode makers and other metallurgical users. name: Hi-Green Carbon Ltd.
business: Hi-Green Carbon recycles end-of-life tyres (ELTs) by pyrolysis, part of the Radhe Group of Energy. Outputs are Recovered Carbon Black (RCB), steel wire, fuel oil and synthesis gas; the syngas is further processed into sodium silicate (raw glass), which is unusual vertical integration for a pyrolysis operator. Certified to ISO 14001:2015, ISO 45001:2018 and ISO 9001:2015. FY26 sales Rs 115 cr. Debtor days of just 23 indicate industrial off-take on short credit rather than tender-based government exposure.
import_substitution: Recovered Carbon Black substitutes virgin/furnace carbon black, of which India is a structural net importer - N-series grades come principally from China, and rubber-grade carbon black has been the subject of Indian anti-dumping duties against China and Russia. RCB from tyre pyrolysis displaces that imported furnace black in non-critical rubber, plastics and masterbatch applications. The displaced product and origin are named, but Hi-Green does not itself publish import-displacement volumes, so this is graded solid on category logic rather than on disclosed tonnage.
moat_note: The closest thing to a regulator-conferred barrier among the environment names here. Waste-tyre pyrolysis in India requires CPCB/SPCB consent under the Hazardous and Other Wastes Rules, and the sector went through a CPCB crackdown that shut a large number of non-compliant units - being an ISO 14001/45001/9001-certified, consented processor is itself the scarce asset. EPR obligations on tyre producers under the 2022 amendment create a regulated demand pool for certified recyclers. Weakness: consent is renewable and replicable by any funded entrant, and the output is a commodity priced off crude and virgin-black spreads.
why_obscure: NSE SME with 2,096 shareholders, zero DII and 0.23% FII. It is filed under Utilities/Waste Management, so it does not surface in either the specialty-chemicals screens (where carbon black lives) or the tyre screens (where its feedstock lives). No analyst covers a Rs 317 cr pyrolysis operator, and half-yearly reporting means only two data points a year.
risk_note: Earnings are a commodity spread, not a service annuity, and it has just gone the wrong way: H2 FY26 PAT collapsed to Rs 2 cr from Rs 7 cr in H1 FY26 and Rs 5 cr in H2 FY25 - a roughly 70% sequential fall in a single half. RCB and fuel-oil realisations track crude and imported virgin carbon black prices, so a soft crude/China-black cycle compresses the spread with no offsetting contract protection. At P/E 37.9 on a shrinking half-year print, the multiple assumes the H2 collapse was transient; nothing in the disclosure establishes that.
liquidity_note: NSE SME, Rs 317 cr cap, 27.85% public float (about Rs 88 cr) over 2,096 holders. Institutional presence is effectively nil. Tradeable in small size only; SME lot sizes and wide spreads apply.
cwip_note: No CWIP at all: Rs 8 cr (Mar 2024) then Rs 0 cr in both Mar 2025 and Mar 2026 against a Rs 56 cr net block. The FY24 project was capitalised and nothing has been started since. This is a company harvesting existing capacity, not building - which is consistent with the flat 14% 3Y sales CAGR and argues against the 'heavy CWIP' preference. Net block of Rs 56 cr on Rs 115 cr of sales means this is genuinely asset-backed, unlike the asset-light services names in this batch, so its 12.6% ROCE is honestly earned rather than flattered by a tiny denominator.
score_rationale: 60/100. Import-sub 13 is the highest of the eight - a named displaced import (virgin/furnace carbon black) with a named origin (China, plus Russia under anti-dumping), which no healthcare name here can claim. Moat 14 not 20: CPCB consent and EPR-driven demand are real regulatory gates, but ROCE of only 12.6% is the tell that the barrier is not converting into returns, and the 20+ band explicitly requires high ROCE. Promoter 12 - 71.92% is above the 55-70% peak band. Institutional 3 (0.23% FII, nil DII). Undercovered 14 on 2,096 holders. Financials only 4: ROE 9.25%, 3Y profit growth negative 12%, and an H2 FY26 PAT collapse to Rs 2 cr.
warnings: 3Y profit growth is NEGATIVE 12% - this is the only keeper with shrinking profits.
H2 FY26 PAT of Rs 2 cr is a ~70% sequential fall from H1 FY26's Rs 7 cr; the P/E of 37.9 does not reflect it.
ROE 9.25% barely clears the >5% gate and is the lowest of the eight.
Commodity spread business - realisations track crude and imported carbon-black prices with no contractual protection.

name: Sejal Glass Ltd.
business: Sejal Glass processes flat glass into toughened, laminated and insulated (IGU) architectural and specialty glass, from plants in Dadra & Nagar Haveli, Taloja (Maharashtra), Erode (Tamil Nadu) and Ras Al Khaimah, UAE. Finished insulated and low-E glazing units are otherwise imported, mainly from China and the Gulf, and Sejal processes them in India instead - but the float glass substrate itself is bought in, frequently imported, so the substitution is of the conversion step, not the material.

name: Spectrum Electrical Industries Ltd.
business: Incorporated 1995, Spectrum manufactures precision electrical press components, engineering-grade injection mouldings and provides surface treatment (plating) for electrical, electronic and automotive stamped parts. It is a tier-1 component and sub-assembly supplier into switchgear, modular wiring accessory and electrical OEM supply chains rather than a branded product company. Net block has grown from Rs 87 cr (FY24) to Rs 146 cr (FY26) with a further Rs 172 cr sitting in CWIP. No customer names are disclosed on the exchange filings reviewed.
import_substitution: Indirect: precision electrical press parts, contacts and moulded sub-assemblies that Indian switchgear OEMs otherwise import from Chinese component vendors. No named imported product or origin country is disclosed, so this is inferred.
moat_note: Tooling ownership plus plating/surface-treatment approval inside an OEM's own BIS-certified switchgear assembly — once a die is qualified into a switch or MCB line, re-sourcing means re-certifying the end product. Real switching cost, but 16.7% ROCE says it is not priced like a monopoly.
why_obscure: NSE SME (Emerge) issuer with only 2,840 shareholders despite a Rs 3,661 cr market cap — the largest coverage gap of any name in this sweep. No concall, no analyst model, and the business description ('injection moulding, press components, surface treatment') reads as generic engineering rather than electronics.
risk_note: Debt-funded capex: D/E is already 1.09 with Rs 172 cr of CWIP still to be commissioned, and screener flags possible interest capitalisation. If the new capacity does not fill, reported ROCE and earnings quality both deteriorate at once.
liquidity_note: NSE SME (Emerge) platform, confirmed via NSE's SME annual-report archive and SME IPO records. Rs 3,661 cr on 2,840 holders and a 23.3% float — the largest market-cap-to-shareholder ratio in this batch and correspondingly thin real turnover.
cwip_note: CWIP has gone 23 -> 38 -> 172 cr across FY24-FY26 and now exceeds the entire Rs 146 cr net block — the company is more than doubling its asset base in a single cycle, the heaviest capital-work-in-progress signal found anywhere in this sweep.
score_rationale: Carried by the capex signal (CWIP 118% of net block) and by having genuine FII participation at 3.63% alongside DII — the only name here where both institutions are meaningfully present. Financials scored only 7/10 despite a 20.4% ROE because D/E of 1.09 is the highest in this batch and ROCE of 16.7% is unexceptional next to the 22-38% peers. Import substitution is generic Make-in-India, hence 8.

name: Nitin Castings Ltd.
business: Incorporated 1982, Maharashtra-based manufacturer of alloy steel castings across static, centrifugal and investment casting routes. Part of the Nitin group promoted by the Kedia family (associated with Nitin Alloys Global). The centrifugal casting line produces heat-resistant alloy tubes and fittings used in petrochemical reformer and cracker furnaces; the static and investment lines serve cement, steel and general engineering. Named customers are not disclosed in public filings.
import_substitution: Centrifugally cast heat-resistant HP/HK-grade alloy tubes and radiant coils for petrochemical reformer furnaces - a category Indian refiners and fertiliser plants have long imported from Schmidt+Clemens (Germany), Kubota (Japan) and Manoir/Duraloy in Europe and the USA. The imported product and origin countries are identifiable, though Nitin does not itself publish an import-substitution claim.
moat_note: Reformer and cracker tubes are a life-safety-critical item - creep-rupture data, metallurgical certification and refinery vendor-list approval gate entry, and a refinery will not change tube supplier between turnarounds. That is a genuine customer-and-inspection-conferred barrier, but the 7% OPM and 15.5% ROCE say Nitin is not currently extracting much of it.
why_obscure: 1,518 shareholders, no institutional ownership disclosed at all, no sell-side coverage, and a Rs.155 cr market cap. The scrip trades under a metals classification, so capital-goods screens skip it entirely.
risk_note: Earnings quality has deteriorated sharply - quarterly PAT fell from Rs.5.71 cr in Jun 2025 to Rs.1.48-1.75 cr across the following three quarters, on a 7% operating margin with only 3% 3-year sales growth. The 31% 3-year profit CAGR is a base-effect artefact, not a trend.
liquidity_note: Mainboard-listed but effectively micro-cap illiquid at Rs.155 cr with 1,518 shareholders; daily traded value is minimal and any meaningful position would move the price.
cwip_note: CWIP appeared at Rs.5 cr in FY26 after two years at nil, equal to 17% of the Rs.30 cr net block - a modest new capacity or line-upgrade project rather than a transformational build.
score_rationale: Moat 14 and import-sub 14 on the reformer-tube niche - the imported product and origins (Schmidt+Clemens Germany, Kubota Japan) are nameable and refinery vendor approval is a real gate; held below 15/20 because Nitin does not disclose which approvals it holds and the 7% OPM suggests weak pricing power. Undercovered 14 on 1,518 shareholders and zero coverage. Institutional 2 - no FII or DII disclosed at all. Financials only 5: 3% sales CAGR, 7% OPM and four consecutive weak quarters.

name: Cupid Ltd
business: Makes WHO/UNFPA-prequalified male and female condoms plus in-vitro diagnostic kits (HIV and Hep-B, CE EU-IVDR certified). Sells largely into donor-funded tender procurement, including the South Africa RT75 programme. Annual PAT is around Rs 108 cr. It has committed Rs 331.53 cr (Rs 82.88 cr deployed) into warrants of Baazar Style Retail, a listed fashion retailer.
moat_note: Company-stated: 'The only Indian manufacturer of female condoms with WHO/UNFPA prequalification' — 'company-stated, narrowly framed enough to be plausible, and WHO/UNFPA PQ lists are public.' Prequalification is a multi-year, audit-heavy gate and donor-funded procurement can only buy from that list. But the note's key qualification: 'stickiness is procedural, not commercial — tenders are re-bid on price among prequalified suppliers, so the switching cost accrues to the list, not to Cupid.' Cupid's own filings show it was eligible for only 75% of prior South Africa female-condom tenders and moved to 100% only after a 2025 PQ upgrade, 'which undercuts a global-monopoly reading.' Veru Inc's FC2 is a direct rival. Certifications: WHO/UNFPA PQ for both male and female condoms, CE EU-IVDR for HIV and Hep-B kits.
pricing_power_note: OPM 25% to 17% to 26% to 30% to 23% to 38% — volatile rather than a controlled series, consistent with the note's view that tenders are re-bid on price. ROCE 33.5% and ROE 27.3%.
import_substitution: Yes, in company-stated form: 'The only Indian manufacturer of female condoms with WHO/UNFPA prequalification' — narrowly framed and plausible, though the note stresses this is prequalification-list membership rather than a global monopoly, with Veru Inc's FC2 a direct rival.
why_obscure: Not obscure at all — 295,432 shareholders; it 'fails everything on size'.
risk_note: The problem, stated first: a P/E around 262 and Rs 331 cr committed to a fashion retailer — Rs 331.53 cr (Rs 82.88 cr deployed) into warrants of Baazar Style Retail by a company earning Rs 108 cr of annual PAT.
v3_gates: Fails everything on size — 295,432 holders.

name: Star Imaging and Path Lab Ltd.
business: West Delhi diagnostics chain tracing back to a 1978 X-ray clinic, incorporated 2004 and converted to a limited company in 2024. Runs 24 diagnostic centres with 236 staff across Delhi, Uttar Pradesh and Nashik (Maharashtra), covering radiology (MRI, CT, mammography, 4D ultrasound), pathology, cardiology and neurology; 7.1 lakh tests were performed in FY26. Revenue splits B2G 54% (Rs 47.3 cr from government PPP radiology contracts, 18 centres), B2C 37% (Rs 33.0 cr from retail Delhi centres), B2B 9% (Rs 8.1 cr from 100+ private-hospital tie-ups including RG Stone/RG Hospital). FY26 revenue Rs 88.5 cr, EBITDA Rs 33.2 cr (37.5% margin), PAT Rs 19.3 cr. Empanelled with CGHS; Tilak Nagar upgraded to a 640-slice CT and Vikaspuri to MRI+CT.
import_substitution: None - domestic clinical services play. The MRI, CT and 640-slice scanners it operates are themselves imported capital equipment.
moat_note: The strongest regulator-conferred position in this batch: NABL and NABH accreditation plus ISO 15189:2012, AERB licensing for every radiation-emitting installation, and PNDT clearance which management describes as taking roughly three months before construction can even start and a further licence cycle before machines can be bought and installed. On top of that sit multi-year government PPP radiology concessions covering 18 of the 24 centres - contracted, exclusive-territory volume that a new entrant cannot bid into mid-term. 26-29% ROCE against that licensed base is exactly the evidence the top band requires.
why_obscure: BSE SME board with only 773 registered shareholders and a 2025 listing. It reports half-yearly, so it produces two result events a year, and there is no sell-side coverage - the only public management commentary is a single self-hosted earnings call. At Rs 162 cr market cap it is invisible next to Lal PathLabs, Metropolis and Vijaya.
risk_note: Trade receivables stood at Rs 49.9 cr at March 2026 against FY26 revenue of Rs 88.5 cr - 206 days, and essentially all of it is the B2G book, which is 54% of revenue. Management admitted on the FY26 call that government payment cycles are the reason operating cash flow was negative Rs 2.6 cr in FY25 before recovering to Rs 23.4 cr in FY26. A single state PPP counterparty stretching payments a further two quarters would consume the entire Rs 31 cr net cash position and force borrowing against the planned Rs 20-25 cr FY27 capex.
liquidity_note: BSE SME with 773 shareholders - lot-size trading and negligible daily turnover despite a healthy 5.73% DII line. The 8.4x P/E partly reflects that no institution can build or exit a position here. Assume you are locked in.
cwip_note: CWIP nil across Mar 2024, Mar 2025 and Mar 2026 - diagnostic equipment is capitalised on installation rather than built, so net block moved Rs 22 cr / Rs 21 cr / Rs 25 cr with no work-in-progress. Note this understates the pipeline: management guided to Rs 20-25 cr of FY27 capex for new centres (Dwarka opening H1 FY27) that has not yet hit the balance sheet.
guidance_quote: While we are guided for 30%-35% growth, certain regulatory delays beyond our control impacted execution this year. However, with those issues now resolved, we remain confident of delivering 25%-30% growth in FY27. ... [on FY28] Around 25% to 30% growth ... Around 110 to 120 [crore].
guidance_source: Pawan Gupta, Chairman & Managing Director - Star Imaging and Path Lab Ltd H2 FY26 and FY26 Earnings Conference Call transcript, 25 May 2026 (filed with BSE 27 May 2026, scrip 544482). Corroborated in the FY26 investor presentation of 25 May 2026: 'Growth Rate for the upcoming years would be 25-30% on YOY'.
score_rationale: Moat 18/25: NABL + NABH + ISO 15189 accreditation, AERB and PNDT licensing per installation, and government PPP concessions covering 18 of 24 centres - genuinely regulator-conferred and backed by 26-29% ROCE. Held just below 20 because the PPP contracts are finite-term and re-tendered, so the barrier renews rather than compounds. Import-sub 0/20: none, and that is entirely appropriate for a diagnostics chain. Promoter 13/15: 71.92%, no disclosed pledge, just above the peak band. Institutional 9/15: DII 5.73% is squarely in range but FII 0.61% is token, so only one real leg. Undercovered 15/15: 773 holders, BSE SME, one self-hosted call, zero analyst coverage. Financials 9/10: ROE 23.7%, D/E 0.21, net cash, 224% 3Y profit CAGR (off a small FY23 base). Only keeper in this batch with an explicit, quotable management growth guidance.

name: L. T. Elevator Ltd.
business: Manufactures passenger, goods, hospital and home elevators from an ISO 14001:2015 certified plant in West Bengal and sells/installs them turnkey through 21 offices nationally; automated car-parking systems sit in subsidiary ParkSmart Solutions Ltd. Customers are described as real-estate developers, hospitals, premium residential projects and government institutions - none individually named in the filings reviewed. FY26 consolidated revenue was Rs 111.3 cr against Rs 54.7 cr in FY25 per the 8 May 2026 audited filing.
import_substitution: Weak. Small Indian lift OEMs displace fully-imported Chinese and Korean elevator packages at the low- and mid-rise end. But Indian assemblers, including this one, typically still import traction machines, controllers and door operators from China, so the substitution is at the package level rather than the component level.
moat_note: This is the closest thing to a regulator-conferred annuity in the batch: state Lifts and Escalators Acts require registration of every installed lift, periodic statutory inspection by the state electrical inspectorate, and in practice a maintenance contract. Every unit sold seeds a recurring AMC, and an installed lift is effectively single-vendor for service life. The offset: there are 100+ Indian lift assemblers, most bought-in components, and the OEM-qualification barrier is low.
why_obscure: BSE SME listed September 2025, 1,179 shareholders, reports half-yearly, and is tagged 'Heavy Electrical Equipment' rather than as an elevator company. Only four half-year columns exist since listing.
risk_note: Debtor days of 171 and working capital days of 184 on a Rs 111 cr revenue base - real-estate developer receivables are the single biggest risk, and at 62.5x earnings the stock is priced for the 86% profit CAGR to continue while the balance sheet is already funding a 6-month cash cycle.
liquidity_note: BSE SME, lot-size trading, listed less than a year. DII at 12.95% with zero FII on a 1,179-holder register - the tradable float is very small and the stock listed at a large premium to issue price.
cwip_note: Nil CWIP at Mar 2024, Mar 2025 and Mar 2026 against a Rs 14.6 cr net block - revenue doubled in FY26 with no visible capex project, which means the growth is coming from assembly throughput and outsourced components, not owned capacity.
score_rationale: Moat at 16 because statutory lift inspection regimes plus a per-unit AMC annuity are a genuine regulator-conferred recurring revenue stream, backed by 17.5% ROCE - held below 20 because the company assembles bought-in components and the Indian lift market has a hundred competitors. Promoter 56.78% sits in the peak band. Institutional score capped at 9 because only DII is present (12.95%) with zero FII, failing the both-sides test. Financials good but the receivable cycle and 62.5x multiple restrain the score.

name: Pitti Engineering Ltd.
business: Makes the components that go inside electric motors and generators - electrical steel laminations, fully assembled stator/rotor packs, machined shafts, castings and fabricated parts. Backward integrated from steel slitting and press tooling through to die-cast rotor and machined assembly. It is entirely a build-to-print supplier to OEMs; it owns no brand. End markets are industrial and traction motors, railways, wind and DG sets rather than fans and small appliances, so the fit with the appliance-component brief is by capability, not by current mix.

But the electrical steel itself (CRNO/CRGO) is still substantially imported into India, so the substitution is at the fabricated-component level, not the raw material.
moat_note: OEM qualification: a motor OEM specifies a lamination geometry, tools it, PPAP-approves the supplier and then cannot change source without re-validating the motor. Combined with owning the press tools and the slitting line, this creates real switching cost - the reason a build-to-print fabricator holds a 16% OPM. Contestable at the low end, hard at the assembled stator/rotor end.
why_obscure: It is the least obscure name in this file - 37,224 shareholders and DII at 20.1% means domestic funds already own it. It is under-followed only in the sense that it is filed by most screens under industrial fabrication rather than consumer durables, and the appliance/motor-component read-through is not the way the street frames it.
