name: Tejas Cargo India Ltd.
business: Faridabad (Haryana) based long-haul surface transportation company providing full-truckload supply-chain movement across India on an owned-fleet model. The Rs 190 cr gross fixed-asset block is essentially trucks and trailers; the company has been adding fleet through debt, with Rs 19-20 cr of vehicles in CWIP in each of the last two years. Listed on NSE Emerge; results are half-yearly.
import_substitution: None - domestic demand play. Trucking capacity for domestic freight; the trucks themselves are bought from Indian OEMs.
moat_note: There is essentially no structural barrier. What exists is scale of owned fleet (which lets it bid national FTL contracts that broker-model players cannot underwrite), driver network and route density. No licence, no approval, no certification gate. This is the low end of the moat scale by design.
why_obscure: 206 registered shareholders is one of the smallest holder bases on the entire board; NSE SME listing, half-yearly reporting, no coverage, and a name indistinguishable from hundreds of private transporters.
risk_note: Borrowings Rs 220 cr against equity of about Rs 193 cr on an asset-heavy fleet earning 12.1% ROCE - barely above the cost of that debt. H2 FY26 PAT fell to Rs 8 cr from Rs 13 cr in H1 FY26 while the fleet (and interest cost) grew, so a diesel spike or a freight-rate soft patch converts thin spread into losses. The stock trades at 48x for a business whose returns are within a couple of points of its borrowing rate.

name: Indian Sucrose Ltd.
business: Punjab-based integrated sugar producer (Oswal group), incorporated 1990, manufacturing and refining white crystal sugar with a 59.50 MW bagasse cogeneration facility. FY26 revenue ₹511cr and PAT ₹31cr at a 15% operating margin — the highest margin in this batch's ethanol/sugar pair. No customers are named; sugar is sold into the regulated release/domestic trade channel and to bulk institutional buyers.
import_substitution: None — domestic demand play, and in fact the opposite: Indian sugar economics are set by the government's MSP, export quota and cane-diversion policy, not by import competition.
moat_note: Cane command-area reservation is the only barrier worth naming: state law ties growers within a mill's reserved area to that mill, giving a local monopsony over cane supply, and a 59.5 MW cogen plant with a PPA monetises bagasse that has no alternative buyer. Both are conferred by regulation and both can be re-priced by the same regulator (SAP, power tariff).
why_obscure: BSE-listed Punjab sugar mill, 19,884 shareholders, zero institutional ownership, no concall, no dividend, and a 3.7x P/E that the market clearly does not believe is sustainable.
risk_note: Policy and cane-cost squeeze in a levered, seasonal business: borrowings ₹192cr against ₹292cr of equity (D/E 0.66) and debtor days already stretched from 81 to 115. Quarterly PAT ranges from -₹3.7cr (Sep 2025) to +₹36.0cr (Mar 2025); Jun 2026 was ₹0.36cr. A Punjab SAP increase not matched by sugar realisations, or an adverse ethanol/diversion policy shift, converts a ₹31cr profit year into a loss year — FY26's 15% margin is a good-cycle number, not a normal one.
liquidity_note: BSE microcap, ₹155cr, ~1.73cr shares outstanding with 35% public float — thin, and the stock is down 6-13% over the past year despite the low multiple, which tells you who is willing to buy it.
cwip_note: CWIP flat at ₹2cr across Mar 2024, Mar 2025 and Mar 2026 — 1% of net block. There is no capex cycle here; earnings are a pure function of the sugar and cogen spread on an existing asset base.
guidance_source: Trendlyne document search for 'Indian Sucrose management revenue growth guidance FY27 outlook distillery ethanol expansion' returned no Indian Sucrose management document — the company does not hold earnings calls and no forward statement could be located.
score_rationale: Cane-area reservation and a cogen PPA are regulatory, but sugar is the textbook policy-priced commodity and the brief says bulk ethanol/sugar deserves under 8 — 7/25. No import substitution, 2/20. Promoter 64.48% is squarely in the peak band and stable, 13/15. FII nil, DII 0.03%, 3/15. 19,884 holders and no coverage but a long BSE history, 8/15. ROE 15.8% and 13% 3Y profit CAGR are strong, tempered by D/E 0.66 and stretched debtors, 7/10. Total 40.

name: Artemis Electricals and Projects Ltd.
business: Manufactures LED lights and lighting fixtures out of Vasai, Thane, and also takes electrical work contracts. It runs a dual model - contract manufacturing for OEMs including Bajaj, and its own brand pushed through roughly 62 distributors across five states. Described in its own filings as product design, procurement, turnkey manufacturing and repairs/maintenance. On the evidence of a Rs 13 cr net block, the physical operation is LED module and luminaire assembly; the LED chips, drivers and power supplies will be imported.
import_substitution: Weak and worth stating plainly. It assembles finished LED luminaires in India in place of finished fixtures imported from China, but the LED packages and the constant-current drivers inside them are Chinese-sourced - Indian LED assemblers almost universally buy chip-on-board and driver modules from Chinese suppliers. The India value-add is housing, heat sink, driver mounting, wiring and BIS-marked assembly, not the light-emitting or electronic content.
moat_note: The only defensible element is OEM qualification - being an approved lighting vendor to Bajaj requires audit, BIS registration under the compulsory registration order for LED luminaires, and photometric/LM-80 test data. That is a real filter. But the distributor network is only 62 accounts across five states and the 12.9% ROCE does not evidence pricing power, so this sits well below a brand-plus-distribution moat.
why_obscure: A Rs 14 stock with 18,850 shareholders, zero institutional ownership, no earnings call, no investor presentation and no analyst coverage - a document search returns only its statutory results filing. It is genuinely unfollowed, but the reason is as much perceived quality as neglect.
risk_note: Capital work-in-progress of Rs 56.5 cr has sat essentially unchanged for two full years (Rs 55.55 cr at Mar 2025, Rs 56.54 cr at Mar 2026) against a net block of just Rs 13.1 cr - i.e. more than four times the operating asset base is parked in an asset that has not been commissioned and is generating no depreciation and no revenue. Trade receivables simultaneously rose 64% to Rs 39.6 cr. If that CWIP is impaired it exceeds five years of current net profit.
liquidity_note: BSE and NSE listed with 18,850 shareholders, but at a Rs 14.1 price on a Rs 355 cr market cap the register is retail-only with zero institutional participation - traded value exists but there is no institutional bid to exit into.
cwip_note: The heaviest CWIP-to-net-block ratio in the file at 430%, but read it as a warning rather than a growth signal: Rs 25.84 cr (Mar24) -> Rs 55.55 cr (Mar25) -> Rs 56.54 cr (Mar26). The balance has been static for a year, which means capital was spent and then stopped converting. Confirmed against the audited consolidated balance sheet filed 28 May 2026 (capital work in progress Rs 5,654.24 lakh vs property, plant and equipment Rs 1,101.34 lakh).
score_rationale: Passes every hard gate and carries the largest CWIP-to-net-block ratio in the sweep, which is why it is here. But scored low across the board: moat 7 because this is LED luminaire assembly on imported chips and drivers with a 62-distributor network; institutional 2 for literally zero FII and zero DII; undercovered 9 rather than 13-15 because 18,850 holders is a wide retail register, not a hidden name. This is the weakest-quality keeper in the file and is included with that stated.

name: Manoj Ceramic Ltd.
business: A distributor, not a manufacturer. Incorporated 1991, it trades ceramic and vitrified tiles and tile adhesives under the MCPL brand, sourcing product from third-party Morbi manufacturers, and has been moving up-market into imported natural marble (the Marmi Bella range) and engineered quartz (NextGen Quartz). It runs a cutting, polishing and customisation facility at Upper Thane that lets it sell customised tile and slab rather than catalogue product. Channels are dealers, own showrooms, exports and direct B2B to architects, builders and contractors; over 1,000 SKUs. No individual customers are named in filings.
import_substitution: None - and in the wrong direction. Its premium growth engine, the Marmi Bella range, is explicitly described by management as 'a premium segment of natural imported marbles'. The company is an importer of finished stone, so it benefits from import liberalisation rather than from substitution.
moat_note: There isn't one, and it should be scored that way. This is a trading and finishing operation with a Rs 5 cr net block. The only differentiator management itself claims is the ability to offer customised designs off the Upper Thane cutting line rather than the standard product 'available in the market'. That is a service differentiator with a season's half-life, not a barrier.
why_obscure: The most extreme case in this batch - a BSE SME with just 395 shareholders on record, half-yearly reporting, and a market cap of Rs 139 cr. It does host earnings calls, but almost nobody is on the register.
risk_note: This is a working-capital business masquerading as a growth story: Rs 71 cr of borrowings against a Rs 5 cr net block funds inventory and receivables. Receivable days were 161 in FY25 and blew out to 220 in H1 FY26 before being pulled back to 111 in FY26. At D/E of 1.32, a repeat of that H1 receivable stretch - one bad season of builder collections - is a genuine liquidity event, not a working-capital wobble.
liquidity_note: BSE SME with only 395 registered shareholders and a Rs 139 cr market cap - the thinnest name in this batch. Trading is lot-based and effectively episodic; treat any position as illiquid.
cwip_note: CWIP nil across Mar 2024, 2025 and 2026 against a Rs 5 cr net block. There is no capex programme - growth is being funded through inventory and receivables, which is the risk described above rather than an asset build.
guidance_quote: So we have already announced that the CAGRs of 25 to 30% have has been maintained before right from our first earning call after getting listed and we have kept the promises and the promise keeps on continuing in the same manner. And for which the required steps that are required for introducing new products, new depots, new horizons have already are all scheduled.
guidance_source: Dhruv Rakasiya, Manoj Ceramic Ltd. earnings call, 3 June 2026, answering a direct question on what volume growth and margin improvement to expect in FY27 (retrieved via Trendylene document search, doc id 2184886).
score_rationale: Scored low deliberately - it passes the hard gates but there is no moat and no import-substitution story, and inflating either would misrepresent it. Moat 5, below the commodity threshold: a Rs 5 cr net block distributor with a polishing line. Import substitution 0 - it imports marble, it does not displace imports. Promoter 11: 53.1% is just under the productive band and warrants were converted recently, so effective control is fresh rather than long-standing. Institutional 8 - FII 2.30% and DII 0.66% both present but the combined 2.96% is at the very bottom of the band. Undercovered 15, the maximum, on 395 shareholders. Financials only 5: ROE 9.77% is barely above the gate, D/E is 1.32 on a trading balance sheet, and the 40%/48% 3Y growth rates come off a tiny base. Guidance points are not part of this score but the FY27 statement is genuine and cited.

name: Alphalogic Industries Ltd.
business: Incorporated 2020; ISO 14001:2015 and BIFMA certified supplier of custom industrial storage racking and warehouse/automated storage systems, with the filing also describing commerce, trade and distribution activity. Recent disclosed order wins are from Blinkit (quick-commerce warehousing). Critically, net block is only Rs 1.93 cr - this is a design, procurement and installation model with fabrication almost entirely outsourced, so it should be read as an asset-light integrator rather than a rack manufacturer.
import_substitution: Weak to none. Selective-pallet and shuttle racking is fabricated in India; the automation content (shuttles, conveyors, WMS) in Indian warehouse projects is typically imported from China or Europe and Alphalogic is a buyer of it. No named import is displaced.
moat_note: Thin. BIFMA certification is a furniture/racking safety standard that many suppliers hold and does not confer exclusivity; racking is a commoditised fabrication with rack-design software widely available. What Alphalogic actually has is a customer roster in quick-commerce warehousing at a moment when that segment is adding capacity fast - a demand tailwind, not a barrier. Under the scoring rules an outsourced-fabrication integrator sits below 8.
why_obscure: 334 shareholders - the smallest register encountered in this sweep. BSE SME, incorporated only in 2020, reports half-yearly, tagged 'Other Industrial Products'.
risk_note: Rs 1.93 cr of net block against a Rs 150 cr market cap means essentially all production is contracted out - the company owns no manufacturing capability it can defend, and a fabricator that decides to sell direct removes the intermediary. Compounding that, working capital days are 143.6 while debtor days are only 50, meaning cash is stuck in inventory/advances rather than receivables, and the filing notes Rs 2.06 cr of other income inside earnings on a base of roughly Rs 3.9 cr of full-year PAT.
liquidity_note: BSE SME with a 334-holder register and 73.81% promoter holding - the tradable float is a few dozen crore at most. This is the least liquid name in the batch by a wide margin.
cwip_note: Nil CWIP at Mar 2024, Mar 2025 and Mar 2026 and a Rs 1.93 cr net block. There is no capex programme at all - which is exactly why ROCE prints at 28.6% and also exactly why the number should not be read as evidence of a manufacturing moat.
score_rationale: Highest obscurity score possible - 334 shareholders, zero coverage, zero institutions - and the ratios are excellent (ROCE 28.6%, ROE 21.3%, D/E 0.03). But the ratios are a consequence of owning almost nothing: Rs 1.93 cr of net block means fabrication is outsourced, which caps moat at 6 under the trading/assembly rule. Institutional scores 2 (no FII, no DII). Promoter 73.81% is above the peak band. This is the weakest franchise in the batch and is included on gates and obscurity, not on quality of barrier.

name: Tera Software Ltd.
industry: IT infrastructure deployment / BOOT e-governance data infrastructure
business: Hyderabad-based IT infrastructure services company incorporated in 1994 that deploys and operates government-facing IT infrastructure on BOOT (build-own-operate-transfer) contracts - hardware, networking, kiosks and citizen-service outlets across 22 states with over 3,000 outlets. Because the assets are owned and operated over the contract life, it is an infrastructure-deployment business rather than a software house, which is why margins are 15% and ROCE 24.4%. name: Sunflag Iron & Steel Co. Ltd.
industry: Alloy and Special Steel — Long Products
business: Established 1984 and operating since 1989 at Bhandara, Maharashtra, Sunflag is an integrated alloy and special steel long-products maker with roughly 5 lakh MTPA of rolled capacity (FY25 volumes about 4.02 lakh MT). It supplies carbon, free- and semi-free-cutting, spring, bearing and stainless grades as flat bars, round bars, bright bars, billets/blooms and wire rods. Roughly 70-75% of revenue comes from automotive OEMs and their tier-1s for transmission gears, drive shafts, steering systems and bearings; the remaining 25-30% goes to railways, ordnance factories, defence and power. It has recently completed a blooming-mill expansion and commissioned a super-alloy plant (FY22) that is still ramping.
import_substitution: Partial and unproven. The super-alloy plant targets nickel-based and specialty grades that India currently imports for defence, aerospace and power applications, and Sunflag's bearing-steel and free-cutting grades displace imported alloy billet at Indian bearing and gear makers. However, neither the CARE rating rationale nor company disclosure names a specific imported product or origin country, and the super-alloy facility has seen slower-than-expected uptake since FY22 — so the substitution thesis is asserted rather than demonstrated.
moat_note: The real barrier is OEM grade approval: automotive transmission-gear and bearing steels require heat-by-heat qualification at each customer and switching is slow once a grade is approved, which is why customer relationships run decades. But it is contestable — Vardhman Special Steels, Mahindra Sanyo and Kalyani hold overlapping approvals, and the 4% ROCE shows those approvals are not converting into pricing power.

name: Bharat Electronics Ltd
business: Defence electronics PSU under the Ministry of Defence. Radars, sonars, electronic warfare suites, missile electronics, communications and C4I systems, plus a growing non-defence line in electronic voting machines and homeland security. FY26 sales Rs 27,610 cr at 29% operating margin, up from Rs 10,401 cr in FY18 - a 13% sales CAGR with margins that expanded 900 bps over the same period.
moat_note: The strongest structural moat available in Indian listed defence, and it is conferred rather than earned: BEL is a Navratna Defence PSU whose promoter is the Government of India, and a large share of its order book arrives through the nomination route rather than open tender. It is the standing recipient of DRDO transfers of technology, which means the state's own R&D output is productionised here by default. Switching costs are effectively absolute - a radar or EW fit is certified into a platform and cannot be re-sourced without re-certifying the platform.
pricing_power_note: Nominated orders are cost-plus rather than price-competitive, which caps upside but removes the risk of a price war. Margin expansion from 20% to 29% over eight years came from mix and indigenisation, not from raising prices.
import_substitution: Direct and central to the thesis. Every radar, sonar and EW system built here displaces an import that would otherwise come from Israel, France or Russia, and the indigenous content mandates under Atmanirbhar Bharat push that share up rather than down.
risk_note: Single-customer concentration is total - the MoD is effectively the only buyer, so a defence budget squeeze or a procurement freeze hits all of revenue at once. Working capital is heavy: 342-day cash conversion cycle and 265 inventory days. Cash conversion is erratic, CFO/OP fell to 33% in FY25 and 44% in FY26 after three years above 100%. At 49x earnings the multiple already prices in sustained order inflow.
data_note: Market cap, ROCE, ROE and the shareholding split pulled from Screener 2026-08-22. Nine-year P&L, balance sheet and cash flow reviewed.
verify_comment: Graded verified on the strength of external evidence rather than company claims: the Government of India appears as promoter at 51.14% in the shareholding pattern, which establishes the Defence PSU status the moat rests on.

name: Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd
business: India's only integrator of military aircraft and helicopters. Builds the Tejas light combat aircraft, the Dhruv/Prachand/Rudra helicopter family and licence-produced Su-30MKI, and runs the repair-and-overhaul base for most of the Indian Air Force fleet. FY26 sales Rs 33,089 cr at 30% operating margin; other income of Rs 3,743 cr on a large cash pile is a material part of profit before tax.
moat_note: A monopoly by construction. There is no second Indian company that can integrate a fighter airframe, and the barrier is not capital but decades of type certification, flight-test infrastructure and an airworthiness relationship with the certification authorities. The ROH business is arguably the better moat than new-build: once HAL is the designated overhaul agency for a fleet the revenue recurs for the platform's whole service life, independent of new order wins.
pricing_power_note: Contract pricing on major platforms is negotiated with a single customer that knows HAL's cost base in detail, so realised pricing power is far weaker than the monopoly position suggests.
import_substitution: The central instrument of Indian aerospace import substitution. Every Tejas delivered replaces an imported fighter, and the LCA Mk1A and Mk2 programmes are explicitly framed by the state as substitution for foreign procurement.
risk_note: Execution, not demand, is the binding constraint - engine supply from GE has repeatedly slipped and delivery schedules have followed. Inventory days ran to 859 in FY26 and working capital days to 301, both sharply worse than FY24. FII holding has fallen every quarter shown, 12.08% to 9.34%. Profit is flattered by other income on the cash pile; strip it out and the operating business is a smaller contributor than headline PAT implies.
data_note: Financials and shareholding from Screener 2026-08-22, nine-year series reviewed.
verify_comment: Verified via the shareholding pattern: Government of India holds 71.64% as promoter, which is the basis of the DPSU status and the nominated-programme access.

name: Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Ltd
business: Defence shipyard building submarines and surface combatants for the Indian Navy. Delivered the Scorpene-class submarine line under technology transfer from Naval Group, and builds Visakhapatnam-class destroyers and Nilgiri-class frigates. Sales tripled from Rs 4,048 cr in FY21 to Rs 13,006 cr in FY26, with operating margin expanding from 6% to 17%.
moat_note: One of only two Indian yards cleared to build conventional submarines, and the more experienced of the pair. The moat is a physical asset that cannot be replicated quickly - a covered submarine construction hall, a trained welding and integration workforce, and a Naval Group technology relationship built over the Scorpene programme. Naval shipbuilding qualification is a multi-year state process, not a commercial decision.
pricing_power_note: Fixed-price naval contracts with long build cycles mean cost inflation is absorbed rather than passed on, which is why margin moves with programme mix rather than with pricing.
import_substitution: Submarines and destroyers built here replace direct foreign purchase, and the P-75I and follow-on submarine programmes are the largest single import-substitution decisions the Navy makes.
risk_note: The lumpiest financials on this list: quarterly operating margin swung from 3.8% to 26% across the last eight quarters as milestone recognition moved. Cash from operations was negative Rs 2,654 cr in FY26 against Rs 2,102 cr positive the year before, and borrowings rose from Rs 20 cr to Rs 447 cr. Institutional ownership is thin - FII 1.72% and falling. Revenue depends on a handful of programmes, so one delayed award moves the whole year.
data_note: Screener 2026-08-22; nine-year P&L, balance sheet and cash flow reviewed.
verify_comment: Verified via shareholding: Government of India is promoter at 81.22%. The Scorpene technology-transfer relationship is a matter of public procurement record rather than a company marketing claim.

name: Solar Industries India Ltd
business: India's largest industrial explosives manufacturer, supplying mining and infrastructure customers including Coal India, with a defence division that has moved into ammunition, propellants and rocket systems. Roughly a fifth of revenue now comes from defence and the share has been rising.
moat_note: The moat is regulatory before it is industrial. Manufacturing and storing explosives requires licensing under the Explosives Act with siting and safety approvals that take years and are effectively unobtainable near existing capacity, so the incumbent set is closed. On top of that sits a distribution network into mining customers where reliability of supply matters more than unit price. The defence extension into ammunition reuses the same licensed energetic-materials capability, which is why a chemicals company can credibly enter a defence market.
pricing_power_note: Industrial explosives are substantially cost-pass-through on ammonium nitrate, so pricing power in the base business is limited. The defence line carries materially better margins.
import_substitution: Ammunition and propellants made here displace imports that India has historically relied on, and the defence order flow is explicitly aimed at reducing that dependence.
risk_note: At 90x earnings this is the most expensive name on the large-cap list by a wide margin, and the rating assumes the defence mix keeps growing. The base business is exposed to ammonium nitrate prices and to Coal India's offtake. Explosives manufacturing carries genuine catastrophic-accident risk, which is a tail the financials do not show.
data_note: Market cap, ROCE, ROE and PE from the Screener gate screen 2026-08-22; shareholding pattern pulled separately the same day.
verify_comment: Graded company-stated: the explosives licensing barrier is structural and well established, but the defence order book and the claimed defence revenue share rest on company disclosure that was not independently checked in this pass.

name: Cummins India Ltd
business: Manufactures diesel and gas engines and gensets for power generation, industrial and automotive use, and exports engines to the Cummins group worldwide. Majority owned by Cummins Inc of the United States.
moat_note: An installed base moat. Engines sold decades ago still need parts and service, and the aftermarket annuity is both higher-margin and far stickier than new equipment sales. Layered on that is emissions-standard capability: each tightening of CPCB norms forces a redesign that smaller genset makers cannot fund, so regulation has repeatedly consolidated the market toward Cummins. Access to parent R&D means India does not carry the development cost of that compliance.
pricing_power_note: Aftermarket parts pricing is genuinely strong. New genset pricing is competitive against Kirloskar and imported units, so blended pricing power is moderate.
import_substitution: Localised engine manufacture displaces imported units, and the plants also export into the parent's global network, which makes this an import substitute and a manufacturing base at once.
risk_note: Demand is cyclical and tied to data-centre, infrastructure and industrial capex, so a capex pause hits new equipment hard even if aftermarket holds. The parent controls technology and transfer pricing, so minority shareholders do not control the terms on which R&D reaches the Indian entity. At 58x the multiple leaves little room for a cyclical downturn.
data_note: Screener 2026-08-22 - screen ratios plus shareholding pattern.
verify_comment: Company-stated. The installed-base and emissions-compliance argument is a reasoned view from public industry structure, not a claim verified against an external source in this pass.

name: Dixon Technologies (India) Ltd
business: India's largest electronics contract manufacturer, assembling mobile phones, televisions, lighting, washing machines and security devices for global and domestic brands. The single largest beneficiary of the production-linked incentive schemes for mobile handsets and IT hardware.
moat_note: The weakest moat on the large-cap list, and it is listed here for the import-substitution pillar rather than for durability of advantage. Contract manufacturing competes on cost and scale, customers are large enough to dictate terms, and the switching cost sits with Dixon rather than with its customer. What advantage exists is scale, PLI-linked capacity that arrived earlier than rivals', and an approved-vendor position with brands that audit slowly. That is a lead, not a wall.
pricing_power_note: Effectively none. EMS operates on assembly margins of a few percent and passes component cost straight through; ROCE is high because capital turns fast, not because pricing is strong.
import_substitution: The clearest large-cap import-substitution story in the country. Handsets and televisions assembled here directly replace finished imports, and the PLI framework exists precisely to move that value onshore.
risk_note: Promoter holding is 28.55% and has fallen 5.2 points across the eight quarters shown - the lowest and fastest-declining promoter stake on this list, which is why the promoter pillar scores 7. Customer concentration is severe. PLI incentives are time-limited and margins after they lapse are unproven. High ROCE on thin operating margin means any assembly-rate slip flows straight to profit.
data_note: Screener 2026-08-22 - screen ratios plus shareholding pattern.
verify_comment: Company-stated. PLI participation is publicly known, but the customer mix and the post-incentive margin path rest on company disclosure not checked here.

name: Hitachi Energy India Ltd
business: Supplies high-voltage transmission equipment and grid automation - transformers, switchgear, HVDC systems and grid software - to Powergrid, state utilities and renewable developers. Subsidiary of Hitachi Energy, which acquired ABB's power grids business.
moat_note: HVDC is the moat and it is a narrow field globally: only a handful of companies worldwide can deliver a high-voltage direct-current link, and India's renewable build-out requires several of them to move power from Rajasthan and Gujarat to demand centres. Utility qualification cycles are long and failure in service is catastrophic, so incumbents with a reference installed base are rarely displaced. The parent relationship supplies technology the Indian entity does not have to develop.
pricing_power_note: Project pricing on utility tenders is competitive, but HVDC and grid-automation scopes have few qualified bidders, which supports margin on the differentiated end of the portfolio.
import_substitution: Localising HVDC and high-voltage equipment replaces imports on projects that would otherwise be sourced from Europe, China or Korea, and grid equipment is a sector where import dependence is a stated policy concern.
risk_note: At 128x earnings this is the most demanding valuation on the board by a distance and assumes the transmission capex cycle runs for years without interruption. Revenue is concentrated in Powergrid and state utilities, whose ordering is policy-driven and can pause. DII holding has fallen from 12.34% to 6.32% over the period shown even as FII rose. Promoter stake stepped down from 75% to 71.31%.
data_note: Screener 2026-08-22 - screen ratios plus shareholding pattern.
verify_comment: Company-stated. The narrow global HVDC supplier set is well established in industry terms but was not verified against an external source in this pass.

name: Hindustan Zinc Ltd
business: Integrated zinc, lead and silver producer working captive mines including Rampura Agucha, one of the largest zinc deposits in the world. Silver is a major by-product and an increasingly large share of profit. Vedanta group controls 60.71%; the Government of India retains 27.92%.
moat_note: A resource moat, which is the most durable kind and the least replicable: the orebody is where it is, the grade is what it is, and captive mining plus integrated smelting places the company in the lowest quartile of the global zinc cost curve. Cost-curve position is the only defensible advantage in a commodity, and it is real here - ROCE of 69% through a full price cycle is not achievable by a marginal-cost producer. Silver by-product credits lower the effective cost of zinc further.
pricing_power_note: None, and it does not need any. Zinc is priced on the LME and the company is a price taker; the advantage is entirely on cost, not on realisation.
import_substitution: India would otherwise import refined zinc and much of its silver; domestic integrated production displaces that directly, and both metals sit on critical-minerals lists.
risk_note: Governance is the reason this scores 73 rather than higher. The Vedanta parent has a history of dividend and cash extraction that suits the controlling shareholder more than minorities, promoter holding has fallen 4.2 points over the period shown, and the government's residual 27.92% stake is a persistent overhang because any disinvestment tranche prices off the market. Institutional ownership is strikingly thin - FII 2.20% and DII 4.96% - which for a company this size and this profitable is itself a signal worth weighing. Earnings move with the LME zinc price and are outside management control.
data_note: Screener 2026-08-22 - screen ratios plus shareholding pattern.
verify_comment: Verified on ownership and structure: Government of India appears at 27.92% and Vedanta as promoter at 60.71% in the shareholding data. The cost-curve position is an industry-structure judgement, not an audited figure.

name: Schaeffler India Ltd
business: Manufactures bearings, linear guides and precision engine and transmission components for automotive, railway and industrial customers, and exports into the Schaeffler group. Majority owned by the German parent.
moat_note: Bearings are a specification-locked business. A bearing is designed into a gearbox or an axle and validated as part of that assembly, so replacing the supplier means re-validating the machine - the switching cost sits with the customer and it is high. Metallurgy and grinding tolerance are genuinely hard to match, which is why the global bearing industry has consolidated to a handful of names rather than commoditising. Railway approvals add a second qualification layer on top.
pricing_power_note: Moderate and asymmetric: strong in the industrial aftermarket and in railway-approved products, weak in automotive OEM supply where annual price-down clauses are the norm.
import_substitution: Localised bearing manufacture replaces imports from Europe and China in a category where India has historically run a deficit, and railway and industrial grades in particular were import-dependent.
risk_note: Automotive demand cyclicality passes straight through, and OEM contracts carry contractual annual price reductions that require continuous cost-out to offset. The German parent controls technology access and transfer pricing. Shareholder count has fallen steadily from 74,954 to 68,487 across the quarters shown, and FII holding is thin at 4.36%.
data_note: Screener 2026-08-22 - screen ratios plus shareholding pattern.
verify_comment: Company-stated. The design-in switching cost is a well-understood feature of the bearing industry but was not verified against a customer filing here.

name: ABB India Ltd
business: Supplies electrification products, motors and drives, robotics and process automation to industrial, infrastructure and data-centre customers. Subsidiary of ABB Ltd, Switzerland, which holds 75%.
moat_note: Process automation is sticky in a way that switchgear is not. Once a plant's distributed control system is ABB, the engineering, the spares and the operators' training are all specific to it, and replacing it means a shutdown - so the installed base compounds through upgrade cycles rather than being re-tendered. Motors and drives are more contested but benefit from an efficiency-standards ratchet that favours suppliers who can fund redesign. Brand and reference installations matter disproportionately in process industries where downtime cost dwarfs equipment cost.
pricing_power_note: Good in automation and service, thin in commodity electrification products where Indian and Chinese competition is direct.
import_substitution: Local manufacture of drives, switchgear and automation hardware replaces imported equipment across industrial capex, and data-centre electrification is a fast-growing substitution pocket.
risk_note: 102x earnings on a business whose revenue tracks industrial capex is the central risk - the rating assumes a long capex upcycle. Promoter at 75% is at the maximum permitted, so there is no scope for supportive buying and any change can only be downward. FII holding fell from 12.28% to 7.67% across the quarters shown. Order flow is concentrated in a few end-markets that turn together.
data_note: Screener 2026-08-22 - screen ratios plus shareholding pattern.
verify_comment: Company-stated. The installed-base argument reflects industry structure rather than a verified external source.

name: Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers Ltd
business: Kolkata defence shipyard building frigates, corvettes and survey vessels for the Indian Navy and fast patrol craft for the Coast Guard. Also builds portable steel bridges and marine diesel engines. Wholly oriented to government customers.
moat_note: A warship yard is a licensed, inspected and security-cleared facility, and the Navy's qualified builder list is short by design. GRSE's position rests on that clearance plus a delivery record across the Project 17A frigate and anti-submarine corvette programmes. The advantage is not technological superiority so much as being one of a handful of yards the state is willing to place a warship order with, and that list does not lengthen quickly.
pricing_power_note: Effectively none - naval contracts are negotiated with a single buyer on cost-plus or fixed-price terms, so margin depends on execution against a fixed price rather than on pricing.
import_substitution: Domestic warship construction replaces foreign naval purchase directly, and the Navy's stated indigenisation targets make this the intended substitution channel rather than an incidental one.
risk_note: Institutional ownership is the thinnest on the mid-cap list - FII 3.21% and DII 1.93%, together barely 5% - which for a profitable defence yard is worth asking about rather than assuming away. Order flow is entirely government and lumpy; a single programme deferral moves the year. Shareholder count has drifted down over the last four quarters. Yard capacity is physically finite, so growth requires capex or a second facility rather than better utilisation.
data_note: Screener 2026-08-22 - gate screen ratios plus shareholding pattern.
verify_comment: Verified via shareholding: the Government of India is promoter at 74.50%, which establishes the defence PSU status and the qualified-yard position the moat rests on.

name: Tenneco Clean Air India Ltd
business: Manufactures clean-air and emission-control systems - catalytic converters, exhaust systems and after-treatment hardware - for commercial vehicles, passenger cars and off-highway engines in India. Subsidiary of the Tenneco group. Listed in late 2025; FY26 quarterly sales around Rs 1,545 cr.
moat_note: The moat is emissions regulation, and it is real but not permanent. After-treatment hardware is homologated as part of a specific engine-and-vehicle combination, so the supplier is designed in for the platform's life and cannot be swapped without re-certifying the vehicle. Each tightening of Bharat Stage norms resets the engineering problem in favour of suppliers with global catalyst and substrate know-how. ROCE of 60.8% and ROE of 44.4% are exceptional and suggest the design-in position is converting into genuine economics.
pricing_power_note: Automotive OEM supply carries annual price-down expectations, so unit pricing is contested. The offset is that regulation-driven content per vehicle rises with each norm change, which grows revenue without needing price increases.
import_substitution: Localised manufacture of catalytic converters and after-treatment systems replaces imported emission hardware, in a category where the technology has historically been foreign-owned.
risk_note: The structural question is powertrain transition: this business exists because internal combustion engines must be cleaned up, and a genuine shift to battery-electric commercial vehicles removes the product rather than shrinking it. Management is a global parent that controls the technology, so minorities do not set terms. The company listed recently and has a short record as a standalone entity - one full-year comparison is not a trend. Customer concentration among a few vehicle OEMs is high.
data_note: Screener 2026-08-22 - overview ratios and shareholding pattern. Note this company fails the microcap board's gates on size and coverage, which is why it sits on the moat board instead.
verify_comment: Company-stated. The homologation switching cost is a well-understood feature of emission-control supply, but the customer mix and content-per-vehicle claims were not checked against an external source in this pass.

name: Hindustan Copper Ltd
business: The only Indian company with captive copper ore mines, operating deposits in Jharkhand, Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh. Produces copper concentrate and cathode. Government of India holds 66.14%.
moat_note: The moat is mineral rights, not operations. Copper mining leases in India are scarce and effectively unobtainable by a new entrant, and Hindustan Copper holds the ones that exist - which is why it is the only integrated domestic producer rather than one of several. Every other Indian copper smelter must buy imported concentrate, so this is the single company whose input is domestic. Copper is on India's critical minerals list and the strategic importance of that position has risen with electrification demand.
pricing_power_note: None. Copper is an LME-priced commodity and the company is a price taker; the entire advantage is that it owns the ore rather than buying it.
import_substitution: India imports the large majority of its copper concentrate. Domestic mined output substitutes that directly, and expanding mine capacity is the stated rationale for the capex programme.
risk_note: Operationally this is the weakest of the resource names here - mine expansion has repeatedly run behind schedule, and production volumes have historically disappointed against plan. At 46x earnings on a commodity producer the multiple prices in an expansion that has not yet been delivered. Shareholder count more than doubled from 6.4 lakh to 13.1 lakh in two quarters, which is retail crowding into a cyclical. DII holding halved over the period shown, from 9.24% to 4.84%. Earnings track the copper price and are outside management control.
data_note: Screener 2026-08-22 - gate screen ratios plus shareholding pattern.
verify_comment: Verified on ownership: Government of India is promoter at 66.14%. The captive-mine position follows from statutory mineral leases rather than from a company claim.

name: Netweb Technologies India Ltd
business: Designs and builds high-performance computing systems, AI training servers, private cloud and storage hardware under its own Tyrone brand, assembled in India. Customers include research institutions, government bodies and enterprises. Quarterly sales grew 172% year on year in the most recent quarter shown.
moat_note: The advantage is being the domestic option in a category where buying domestic is increasingly a requirement rather than a preference. Government and research procurement of computing hardware carries local-content and security conditions that foreign OEMs cannot always satisfy, and Netweb is one of very few Indian companies that can integrate a supercomputing cluster to specification. System integration know-how in HPC is genuinely non-trivial. But the underlying silicon is bought in, so this is design-and-integration value rather than a technology moat of its own.
pricing_power_note: Moderate. Bespoke HPC and AI cluster builds are specified rather than shopped on price, but component cost is a large and rising share of the bill and is set by others.
import_substitution: One of the cleanest substitution stories available - server and HPC hardware has been almost entirely imported, and both the AI mission and public-procurement local-content rules are explicitly designed to move that onshore.
risk_note: 122x earnings is the second most demanding multiple on the moat board and assumes AI-driven ordering compounds for years. Promoter holding fell 8.5 points over the eight quarters shown, from 71.39% to 66.98% - the steepest decline among the mid caps here. Revenue is lumpy and order-driven, with heavy dependence on government and institutional buyers whose budget cycles can pause. Component supply, particularly GPUs, is outside the company's control and has been the binding constraint industry-wide.
data_note: Screener 2026-08-22 - gate screen ratios plus shareholding pattern.
verify_comment: Company-stated. The domestic-integrator position is plausible from public procurement structure but the customer list and local-content qualification were not independently verified in this pass.

name: Premier Energies Ltd
business: Manufactures solar photovoltaic cells and modules, and is one of the few Indian producers with meaningful integrated cell capacity rather than module assembly alone. Serves domestic developers and the government's rooftop and utility-scale programmes.
moat_note: The advantage here is policy-shaped rather than intrinsic. The Approved List of Models and Manufacturers and the basic customs duty on imported cells create a protected domestic market, and Premier is one of a small number of firms with operating cell lines rather than module assembly using imported cells. Integrated cell capacity is the scarce asset and it takes capital and time to build. The honest caveat is that solar manufacturing is a commodity industry globally, and the moat is the tariff wall plus a capacity head start, not a durable technological edge.
pricing_power_note: Weak in structure, temporarily good in practice. Module prices are set globally by Chinese oversupply; Indian realisations hold up only while duty protection and ALMM sourcing rules bind.
import_substitution: Among the most explicit import-substitution mandates in Indian industrial policy - the entire duty and ALMM framework exists to replace imported Chinese cells and modules with domestic output.
risk_note: The moat is a policy decision and policy can be reversed; any relaxation of duty or ALMM would expose the cost gap against Chinese producers immediately. Promoter holding dropped from 63.94% to 58.48% in the most recent quarter, a 5.5-point fall in one step. Global solar overcapacity is severe and periodically dumps prices. Capacity expansion is capital-hungry in an industry where technology generations turn over quickly, so today's line can be tomorrow's stranded asset.
data_note: Screener 2026-08-22 - gate screen ratios plus shareholding pattern.
verify_comment: Company-stated. The ALMM and duty framework is public policy, but Premier's integrated cell capacity and its position within that framework rest on company disclosure not verified here.

name: Neuland Laboratories Ltd
business: Manufactures active pharmaceutical ingredients and runs a custom manufacturing solutions business synthesising complex molecules for innovator pharmaceutical companies. Revenue splits between a generic API portfolio and CMS work tied to specific customer molecules.
moat_note: The CMS business is the moat and it is one of the better ones in Indian pharma. When an innovator files a drug application, the API manufacturing site and process are named in the regulatory dossier; changing supplier mid-lifecycle means a regulatory filing and a bridging study, so the incumbent is locked in for the molecule's commercial life. That is a switching cost imposed by the regulator on the customer, not a discount offered by the supplier. The generic API book is far more contested and competes with Chinese producers on cost.
pricing_power_note: Strong and durable in CMS where the process is proprietary and the supplier is named in the filing; weak in commodity APIs where price follows Chinese capacity.
import_substitution: Complex API and intermediate manufacture displaces Chinese supply in a category where Indian formulators' dependence on Chinese intermediates is a recognised strategic vulnerability.
risk_note: Promoter holding is only 32.62%, the second lowest on the moat board, and has drifted down. Revenue is concentrated in a small number of CMS molecules, so a single customer's product failing in trials or losing exclusivity removes a large block of revenue at once - this has happened before in the sector and the financials would show it sharply. FII holding fell from 26.46% to 21.08% across the period. At 60x, the multiple assumes the CMS pipeline converts.
data_note: Screener 2026-08-22 - gate screen ratios plus shareholding pattern.
verify_comment: Company-stated. The dossier lock-in is a genuine and well-documented feature of API regulation, but Neuland's specific customer and molecule concentration was not verified against filings here.

name: Indo-MIM Ltd
business: Manufactures precision components by metal injection moulding and investment casting, exporting to automotive, aerospace, medical device and firearms customers worldwide from plants in India. Listed recently; only one quarter of shareholding history is available.
moat_note: Metal injection moulding is a genuinely specialised process - it makes small, complex, high-tolerance parts that neither machining nor conventional casting can produce economically, and the feedstock formulation and debinding/sintering control are hard-won process knowledge rather than purchasable equipment. Parts are qualified into a customer's assembly, particularly in aerospace and medical where requalification is expensive, so the design-in position is sticky. Indo-MIM is one of the larger MIM producers globally, which matters because the customer base is global rather than Indian.
pricing_power_note: Reasonable. MIM parts are specified by geometry and tolerance rather than shopped on price, and the qualified-supplier list per part is short.
import_substitution: Runs in both directions - it substitutes precision components India would otherwise import, while primarily earning from exports, which makes it a manufacturing base as much as a substitution play.
risk_note: The record as a listed company is very short - one quarter of shareholding data - so governance and disclosure quality are unproven and there is no listed history through a downturn. Export concentration means currency and foreign demand risk sit directly on earnings, and firearms and automotive end-markets are cyclical. Institutional ownership is thin at FII 2.34%. Nearly 9.5 lakh shareholders for a recently listed company implies heavy retail participation from the IPO. At 68x the multiple is demanding for a component manufacturer.
data_note: Screener 2026-08-22 - gate screen ratios plus shareholding pattern. Only the Jul 2026 shareholding quarter exists, so no trend can be read.
verify_comment: Company-stated, and weakly so - a recent listing with one quarter of public data. The MIM process barrier is real industrially; the company's relative global position was not verified here.

name: TD Power Systems Ltd
business: Manufactures AC generators and electrical machines for steam, gas, hydro and wind turbine applications, selling to turbine OEMs and power producers in India and export markets.
moat_note: Generators are built to match a specific turbine, so TD Power sells to turbine OEMs who qualify a generator partner and then stay with them across a product family - the qualification is engineering-led and slow. The company's spread across steam, gas, hydro and wind means it is not tied to one generation technology, which in a decarbonising grid is a real structural advantage over single-technology suppliers. The limit is that its customers are large OEMs with the scale to bring generator manufacture in-house if they choose.
pricing_power_note: Moderate and customer-dependent. Selling to a handful of global turbine OEMs means negotiating with well-informed buyers, though bespoke machine design limits direct price comparison.
import_substitution: Domestic generator manufacture replaces imported machines for Indian power projects and also exports into global OEM supply chains.
risk_note: Promoter holding is 26.87%, the lowest on the entire moat board, after falling 7.4 points over the eight quarters shown - and it stepped down sharply in a single quarter. That is the main reason the promoter pillar scores 7. Institutional ownership at 50% combined is high, which cuts both ways: validation, but also crowded positioning that exits quickly. At 87x earnings on a capital-goods business, the multiple assumes a long power capex cycle. Order flow is concentrated among few OEM customers.
data_note: Screener 2026-08-22 - gate screen ratios plus shareholding pattern.
verify_comment: Company-stated. The OEM qualification argument reflects industry structure; the customer concentration and technology spread were not verified against filings here.

name: Himadri Speciality Chemical Ltd
business: Produces coal tar pitch, carbon black, refined naphthalene and speciality carbon products, supplying aluminium smelters, graphite electrode makers and tyre manufacturers, with an expansion into lithium-ion battery anode materials.
moat_note: The base business has a genuine and unglamorous moat: coal tar distillation is pollution-intensive and environmentally permitted, and new consents for this kind of plant are extremely hard to obtain in India, which closes the entrant set. Himadri is the largest domestic coal tar pitch producer and its aluminium-smelter customers cannot easily requalify a pitch supplier because anode quality drives smelter performance. The battery anode-material extension is the interesting part strategically - it applies existing carbon chemistry to a supply chain India currently imports entirely - but it is early and unproven at scale.
pricing_power_note: Limited in the base business, which passes through coal tar and crude derivative costs. The anode-material line, if it reaches commercial scale, would sell into a market with almost no domestic alternative.
import_substitution: Battery anode material is close to 100% imported into India today, principally from China, so domestic production would substitute a strategically sensitive input outright. The existing carbon black and pitch lines also displace imports.
risk_note: The lowest ROCE and ROE on the mid-cap list, at 22.1% and 17.8% - it clears the gates but with less margin than its neighbours. The base business is cyclical and tied to aluminium and tyre demand, with input costs that swing. The anode-materials thesis is the reason for much of the rating and it is a capex and execution promise rather than a delivered business; if it slips, the multiple has little support. DII holding is thin at 3.33%. Environmental compliance is both the moat and the standing risk - the same permitting regime that protects the incumbent can tighten on it.
data_note: Screener 2026-08-22 - gate screen ratios plus shareholding pattern. Promoter holding rose 7.6% over the period shown, which is unusual and favourable.
verify_comment: Company-stated. The permitting barrier is a real feature of the industry; the anode-material capability and timeline rest entirely on company disclosure and are explicitly unproven.

name: APL Apollo Tubes Ltd
business: India's largest producer of structural steel tubes and hollow sections, selling through a distributor network into construction, infrastructure and industrial applications. Operates multiple plants with direct-forming technology.
moat_note: Distribution and scale rather than technology. The product is a commodity by nature, and the advantage is a national dealer network, plant locations close to demand that cut freight on a heavy low-value good, and a scale that lets it price below smaller regional mills. Freight economics are the most defensible part - steel tubes are expensive to move relative to their value, so a plant near the customer has a structural cost advantage that a distant competitor cannot match by being more efficient. This is the weakest moat among the mid caps here and the score reflects it.
pricing_power_note: Limited. Realisations track steel prices with a lag, and the business model is built on volume and conversion spread rather than on pricing.
import_substitution: Marginal, which is why the import-substitution pillar scores only 12. Structural tubes are largely a domestic-supply product; this qualifies as a manufacturer rather than as a substitution play, and `qualifies_as` records only `manufacturer` for that reason.
risk_note: Promoter holding is 28.25% and has drifted down, while FII holding at 35.12% is the highest on the moat board - ownership is dominated by institutions rather than by the founder, which cuts both ways. Earnings are geared to the steel price cycle and to construction demand, and a spread compression hits conversion margin directly. At 48x for a commodity converter the multiple is full. Shareholder count has fallen steadily from 2.18 lakh to 1.59 lakh.
data_note: Screener 2026-08-22 - gate screen ratios plus shareholding pattern.
verify_comment: Company-stated. The freight-economics argument follows from the physical product; the market-share claim was not verified against an external source in this pass.

name: Inox India Ltd
business: Designs and manufactures cryogenic storage and transport equipment - vacuum-insulated tanks, containers and distribution systems for industrial gases, LNG and scientific applications - and supplies cryogenic systems used in space and research programmes. Exports a substantial share of output.
moat_note: Cryogenic containment is an unforgiving engineering discipline: holding liquid gases near absolute zero requires vacuum-insulation know-how where a small design error shows up as boil-off loss, and vessels are built to pressure-vessel codes that require certification of the manufacturer, not just the product. Qualification for space and scientific applications is slower still. The result is a short global list of credible suppliers and a customer base that does not re-tender casually. Exports are the tell - a company selling cryogenic tanks into developed markets is competing on capability rather than on Indian labour cost.
pricing_power_note: Good on engineered and code-certified vessels where the qualified supplier set is small; thinner on standard industrial-gas tanks where regional fabricators compete.
import_substitution: Cryogenic equipment for LNG distribution and industrial gases would otherwise be imported, and the space and research applications substitute supply that has historically come from a handful of foreign specialists.
risk_note: At 68x earnings the multiple assumes the LNG and industrial-gas capex cycle keeps running. Order flow is project-linked and lumpy rather than recurring, so a slow quarter reflects timing as much as demand. Shareholder count fell from 1.83 lakh to 1.40 lakh over four quarters before recovering slightly. The LNG distribution thesis depends on Indian gas infrastructure building out on schedule, which has repeatedly slipped in the past.
data_note: Screener 2026-08-22 - gate screen ratios plus shareholding pattern.
verify_comment: Company-stated. Pressure-vessel certification and the narrow supplier set are real features of the industry; the specific space and research programme relationships were not verified against an external source in this pass.

name: Triveni Turbine Ltd
business: Manufactures industrial steam turbines below 100 MW for captive power, sugar, cement, process industry and waste-heat recovery applications, selling into India and a wide export market with an aftermarket service business alongside.
moat_note: The strongest engineering moat among these small caps. Sub-100 MW industrial turbines are a niche the large turbine makers largely vacated because the unit economics do not suit their cost base, leaving a small global field - and turbine aerodynamics and rotor dynamics are accumulated know-how rather than purchasable technology. The better half of the business is aftermarket: a turbine runs for decades and needs spares, refurbishment and efficiency upgrades from someone who knows the machine, so the installed base is an annuity that grows with every unit shipped. That is a moat that compounds rather than erodes.
pricing_power_note: Genuinely good in the aftermarket, where the original manufacturer is the natural service provider and the customer is comparing against unplanned-downtime cost rather than against a competing quote. New-unit pricing is contested on international tenders.
import_substitution: Domestic turbine manufacture replaces imported industrial turbines, and the export business simultaneously earns foreign exchange in a category India historically imported.
risk_note: FII holding has fallen every quarter shown, from 28.09% to 20.58% - an 7.5-point exit that is worth understanding before buying. Demand is tied to process-industry capex and to sugar and waste-heat projects, all cyclical. Export exposure carries currency and geopolitical risk. At 53x earnings the rating already reflects the aftermarket quality, so execution disappointment would be punished.
data_note: Screener 2026-08-22 - gate screen ratios plus shareholding pattern.
verify_comment: Company-stated. The aftermarket annuity structure follows from the product's service life; the claimed global position in the sub-100 MW niche was not independently verified here.

name: HBL Engineering Ltd
business: Makes specialised industrial batteries - nickel cadmium, lithium and valve-regulated lead acid - for defence, railways, aviation and telecom, and supplies railway electronics including the Kavach train collision avoidance system. Defence batteries serve missile, submarine and aircraft applications.
moat_note: Two moats stacked. The battery business sits in specification-locked niches: a nickel-cadmium pack qualified for an aircraft or a submarine is certified into that platform and cannot be swapped without requalification, and the volumes are too small to attract commodity manufacturers. The railway electronics side is stronger still - Kavach is a mandated safety system with a very short approved-vendor list, and Indian Railways' rollout is a policy commitment rather than a commercial cycle. ROCE of 58% and ROE of 45% on a 24x multiple is an unusual combination and reflects how few competitors reach these approvals.
pricing_power_note: Strong in qualified defence and aviation batteries where alternatives are effectively absent. Kavach pricing is set through railway tendering, so volume rather than price is the lever there.
import_substitution: Defence and aviation batteries in these chemistries were historically imported, and Kavach is explicitly an indigenous replacement for foreign train-protection systems.
risk_note: DII holding is negligible at 0.97% and FII only 5.62%, so institutional validation is almost absent despite the returns - either the market is missing something or the market knows something. Revenue depends heavily on Indian Railways' Kavach ordering pace, which has historically been slower than announced and is a single-customer dependency in all but name. Shareholder count has moved erratically. The defence battery business is small-volume and lumpy.
data_note: Screener 2026-08-22 - gate screen ratios plus shareholding pattern.
verify_comment: Company-stated. Kavach approval and defence qualification are plausible from public railway and defence procurement structure, but neither the approved-vendor status nor the order book was verified against an external source in this pass.

name: KSB Ltd
business: Manufactures centrifugal pumps and industrial valves for power, water, chemicals, oil and gas and building services, including pumps qualified for nuclear power applications. Subsidiary of KSB SE of Germany.
moat_note: Nuclear qualification is the part that matters. A pump certified for nuclear service carries documentation, material traceability and inspection history that takes years to establish and that a customer will not casually re-source, and the qualified supplier list for Indian nuclear projects is short. Outside nuclear, the moat is more ordinary - engineered pumps for chemical and power service are specified into plant designs and supported by a service network, which produces stickiness without exclusivity. The German parent supplies hydraulic design and metallurgy the Indian entity does not fund.
pricing_power_note: Strong in nuclear and engineered process pumps where qualification limits the bidder set; weak in standard water and building-services pumps competing against domestic volume manufacturers.
import_substitution: Domestic manufacture of engineered and nuclear-grade pumps replaces European imports, and India's nuclear expansion programme makes that substitution strategically significant rather than merely commercial.
risk_note: The lowest ROCE among the small caps chosen here at 24.7%, so it clears the gate with less headroom than its neighbours. Nuclear order flow depends on a state programme that has historically moved slowly. The parent controls technology and transfer pricing. Shareholder count fell from 70,326 to 51,832 across the quarters shown. At 53x for a pump manufacturer growing at industrial-capex rates, the multiple is demanding.
data_note: Screener 2026-08-22 - gate screen ratios plus shareholding pattern.
verify_comment: Company-stated. Nuclear qualification is a documented regulatory process in principle, but KSB's specific approvals and their revenue contribution were not verified against an external source in this pass.

name: Vinati Organics Ltd
business: Produces specialty monomers and chemicals, principally ATBS (acrylamido tertiary-butyl sulfonic acid) used in oilfield chemicals, water treatment and personal care, and IBB (isobutyl benzene), the key intermediate for ibuprofen. Largely export-oriented.
moat_note: The clearest single-product global position on this board. Vinati is the dominant world producer of ATBS, a molecule with a small total market that is nonetheless essential to its users - which is precisely the structure that deters entry, because a new entrant would collapse the price of the market it was trying to enter while facing a decade-long customer qualification process. IBB has a similar shape: a specific intermediate where Vinati is a principal global supplier to ibuprofen manufacturers. Small-market dominance is an underrated moat and it is the reason a company of this size earns these returns.
pricing_power_note: Good but not unlimited - customers accept price because the input is a small share of their cost and requalification is expensive, but they resist aggressive increases and can push back through volume negotiation.
import_substitution: India would otherwise import these monomers and intermediates; more importantly the company exports them, so this is a case of Indian chemistry supplying the world rather than merely displacing imports at home.
risk_note: Single-product concentration is the mirror image of the moat - ATBS demand tracks oilfield activity, and an oil capex downturn hits the best product hardest. Returns have compressed: ROCE of 21.3% and ROE of 16.2% are the weakest among the small caps chosen and well below this company's own history, which suggests either pricing pressure or capacity running below plan. FII holding fell from 5.48% to 3.65%. Shareholder count has declined steadily. Customer concentration in oilfield chemicals is high.
data_note: Screener 2026-08-22 - gate screen ratios plus shareholding pattern.
verify_comment: Company-stated. The global ATBS share is a company claim repeated widely in industry commentary but not verified against an independent source in this pass - it should be treated as unconfirmed until it is.

name: Quality Power Electrical Equipments Ltd
business: Manufactures high-voltage electrical equipment for power grids - reactors, harmonic filters, capacitor banks and instrument transformers - used in HVDC transmission and grid stabilisation, with a meaningful export order book.
moat_note: Sits in the same scarce niche as the large-cap HVDC names but as a component specialist rather than a system integrator. Reactors and harmonic filters for HVDC links are engineered to a specific project's electrical parameters and must be type-tested at independent high-voltage laboratories, which is expensive and slow enough to keep the qualified supplier list short worldwide. Exports are the evidence that the qualification is genuine rather than domestic protection. The dependency is that it sells into projects led by others, so it captures a slice rather than setting the terms.
pricing_power_note: Reasonable on type-tested HVDC components where few suppliers qualify, weaker on standard capacitor and transformer products.
import_substitution: Grid stabilisation equipment for Indian transmission projects would otherwise be imported from Europe, China or Korea; domestic supply of type-tested reactors and filters replaces that directly.
risk_note: Recently listed with only six quarters of shareholding history, so governance and disclosure are not yet proven across a cycle. At 76x earnings on an order-driven capital-goods business the multiple assumes flawless execution of the grid capex cycle. Institutional ownership is thin - FII 3.37%, DII 6.45%. Shareholder count swung from 81,106 down to 58,129 and back to 85,706, which is unusual churn. Revenue depends on transmission project awards that can be deferred by policy.
data_note: Screener 2026-08-22 - gate screen ratios plus shareholding pattern. Only six quarters of shareholding data exist.
verify_comment: Company-stated, and with a short listed record. Type-testing requirements are a genuine industry barrier; this company's specific qualifications and export customers were not verified here.

name: Kennametal India Ltd
business: Manufactures tungsten carbide cutting tools, wear parts and tooling systems for machining, mining and general engineering customers, plus machine tools and services. Subsidiary of Kennametal Inc of the United States.
moat_note: Cutting tools are a consumable sold on productivity rather than price - a tool that lasts longer or cuts faster pays for itself in machine time, so customers who have proven a grade in their process are slow to switch. Carbide grade metallurgy and coating technology are the hard part and sit with the global parent. The business also has an inherent razor-and-blade quality: tooling systems get designed into a customer's machining process and the inserts recur for the life of that process. What limits the score is that Chinese and Indian carbide producers compete hard at the commodity end.
pricing_power_note: Good in engineered and coated grades where the productivity argument holds; contested in standard inserts where cheaper carbide is a genuine substitute.
import_substitution: Domestic carbide tooling manufacture replaces imports in a category where India has run a persistent deficit, particularly in coated grades and application engineering.
risk_note: Demand is a direct read on Indian manufacturing activity and machining volumes, so it turns with the industrial cycle and has no defensive characteristics. FII holding has collapsed to 0.23% from an already thin 0.91%. Only 12,110 shareholders - by far the least widely held name on the moat board, which means liquidity is poor and a position is hard to exit at scale. The US parent controls technology and pricing, and 75% ownership leaves a small float.
data_note: Screener 2026-08-22 - gate screen ratios plus shareholding pattern. Note the very low shareholder count, which would comfortably pass the microcap board's coverage gate if size permitted.
verify_comment: Company-stated. The consumable stickiness argument reflects industry structure rather than a verified external source.

name: Sandur Manganese & Iron Ores Ltd
business: Mines manganese and iron ore from captive leases in Karnataka and has integrated downstream into ferroalloys and coke, with a steel-making expansion. Manganese is a critical input to steel and its domestic supply is limited.
moat_note: A mineral-lease moat, and in India that is the hardest kind to replicate: mining leases are granted by the state through auction and are effectively unobtainable outside that process, so an incumbent with long-dated captive manganese reserves holds an asset no amount of capital creates. Manganese matters more than its volume suggests because there is no substitute for it in steel making and Indian domestic supply is thin. Downstream integration into ferroalloys captures the conversion margin rather than selling ore away, which is what lifts returns above a pure miner's.
pricing_power_note: None - ore and ferroalloy prices are set by global markets and Chinese demand. The advantage is entirely captive input cost.
import_substitution: India imports a significant share of its manganese requirement; domestic mined and converted output substitutes that, and manganese appears on critical-minerals lists for exactly this reason.
risk_note: Institutional ownership is effectively nil - FII 1.73% and DII 0.58%, which is why this is the only tier 2 name on the moat board. Earnings are fully exposed to manganese and iron ore price cycles and to steel demand, with no pricing lever at all. The steel-making expansion is a large capital commitment into a competitive industry and takes the company away from the mining asset that is the actual moat - execution risk here is the main thing to watch. At 13x the multiple is the cheapest on the moat board, which is the market pricing the cyclicality rather than an oversight.
data_note: Screener 2026-08-22 - gate screen ratios plus shareholding pattern.
verify_comment: Company-stated. Mining leases are statutory and therefore externally established in principle, but the specific lease tenure and reserve position were not verified against filings in this pass.

name: Esab India Ltd
business: Manufactures welding consumables - electrodes, wires and fluxes - and welding and cutting equipment, sold through a national distributor network to fabrication, shipbuilding, construction and general engineering customers.
moat_note: A consumables-and-distribution moat rather than a technological one. Welding consumables are specified by welding procedure qualification: a fabricator qualifies a procedure using a particular electrode, and in code-governed work such as pressure vessels or shipbuilding, changing consumable means requalifying the procedure. That makes an approved consumable sticky in exactly the applications that matter most. Underneath sits a distribution network reaching thousands of small fabricators, which is expensive and slow to build. ROCE of 64.7% and ROE of 48.8% with essentially no capital intensity is the economic signature of a consumables business with brand pull.
pricing_power_note: Good in code-qualified and specialty consumables, moderate in general-purpose electrodes where local manufacturers compete on price and the distributor decides.
import_substitution: Domestic consumable manufacture replaces imported welding materials, particularly in specialty alloys and code-approved grades.
risk_note: Demand is a straightforward proxy for Indian fabrication and construction activity and turns with it. The strategic pillar scores only 7 because welding consumables, while essential, sit outside the defence and critical-infrastructure framing the moat board is built around. Only 20,083 shareholders means thin liquidity. FII holding is negligible at 1.62%. Raw material costs - steel wire and alloying elements - pass through with a lag that compresses margin when input prices rise quickly.
data_note: Screener 2026-08-22 - gate screen ratios plus shareholding pattern.
verify_comment: Company-stated. Welding procedure qualification is a genuine code requirement; the company's share of approved consumables was not verified against an external source here.

name: Shilchar Technologies Ltd
business: Manufactures distribution and power transformers, including units for renewable energy projects, with a growing export business to North America and Europe.
moat_note: The weakest moat on the small-cap list and the score says so. Transformers are a competitive product made by many Indian manufacturers, and the barrier is execution and testing capability rather than anything structural. What advantage exists is real but narrow: export qualification to North American and European standards requires type testing and customer audits that most domestic peers have not undertaken, and the renewable-project segment values on-time delivery highly enough to favour proven suppliers. ROCE of 50.7% reflects a tight capacity cycle with strong current demand, not a durable position - and returns like that in a competitive product invite capacity.
pricing_power_note: Currently good because global transformer capacity is tight and lead times are long, but this is cycle pricing rather than structural pricing power and will normalise when capacity catches up.
import_substitution: Domestic transformer manufacture substitutes imports for Indian grid and renewable projects, though the more interesting part of the story is exports rather than substitution.
risk_note: The core risk is that today's returns are a capacity-shortage artefact. Global transformer lead times are long right now and everyone is adding capacity; when it lands, both pricing and ROCE compress. Promoter holding fell 3.7 points, from 64.01% to 62.12%. Institutional ownership is minimal at 4.5% combined. This is the smallest company on the moat board at Rs 4,442 cr, sitting just above the small-cap floor, so it carries more single-customer and single-plant concentration risk than its neighbours.
data_note: Screener 2026-08-22 - gate screen ratios plus shareholding pattern. Sits just above the Rs 4,000 cr boundary between micro and small.
verify_comment: Company-stated. Export qualification is plausible from the revenue mix but neither the certifications nor the customer list were verified in this pass.

name: Jenburkt Pharmaceuticals
theme_detail: Branded domestic formulations, not API — placed in the pharma theme because the board has no separate formulations bucket.
business: Branded generic formulations sold into the domestic prescription market through its own field force — orthopaedic, dermatology and nutraceutical ranges are the disclosed spine of the business. Nine years of Screener-visible accounts: sales Rs 115 cr (FY18) to Rs 169 cr (FY26), a compound rate in the mid single digits, so this is a slow, self-funded compounder rather than a growth story. Fixed assets are small (Rs 19 cr) against Rs 46 cr of CWIP, which is a new plant being built out of accruals rather than borrowings.
moat_note: Jenburkt makes no monopoly, 'only-in-India' or first-mover claim anywhere in its disclosure, so there is nothing to grade — hence 'none claimed' rather than a grade. What the numbers do support, and it is the strongest single piece of evidence in this week's microcap batch, is durable pricing power: operating margin has held between 17% and 27% across nine consecutive years spanning COVID, the 2021-23 API cost spike and two rounds of NLEM price revision, and ROCE has not fallen below 24% in that period. That is the signature of a prescriber-relationship moat in branded generics — the doctor writes the brand, the patient does not substitute, and the field force is the asset.
